records.descriptionEn: IAT sensor 3 bank 2 signal voltage below expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: IAT sensor 3 bank 2 signal voltage above expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from IAT sensor 3 on bank 2. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Humidity Sensor Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: Open circuit at the humidity sensor (used by ECU for combustion correction, especially on direct-injection engines).

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Humidity Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Humidity sensor reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Humidity Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Humidity sensor signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Humidity Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Humidity sensor signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Humidity Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from humidity sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The relationship between barometric pressure and turbo inlet pressure (bank 2) is implausible — at engine off the two should match. Indicates an inlet sensor or barometric sensor fault.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Generic electrical fault on turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A (post-compressor pressure measurement).
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A reading implausible. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from turbo outlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Battery B State of Charge Performance
records.descriptionEn: State of charge of battery B (typically auxiliary or hybrid battery) shows performance fault — does not behave according to charging model.

records.titleEn: EVAP System Tank Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP tank vapor line is restricted or blocked. Tank pressure cannot equalize properly. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
records.descriptionEn: The Body Control Module (BCM) sent a request to the engine ECU to illuminate the MIL — actual fault is in a body system; this is a forwarded request, not a powertrain fault.

causes.labelEn: Underlying BCM fault — read BCM codes

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit. The signal is missing, out of plausible range, or the wiring shows continuity issues. Used as a generic fault when no more specific MAF code applies.

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The mass air flow (MAF) sensor signal is outside the expected range or does not track engine load plausibly. The ECU compares MAF readings against load calculated from RPM, throttle position and intake pressure; persistent disagreement triggers this code.

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value below the plausible minimum for current engine speed and load. The ECU substitutes a calculated load value while the fault is active.

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value above the plausible maximum for current engine speed and load. Often indicates a sensor that is failing in a way that produces excess output, or a short to supply voltage in the signal path.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts or noise on the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit. The fault is not constantly present, suggesting a loose connection, intermittent wiring break, or a failing sensor under specific conditions (vibration, temperature).

records.titleEn: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) or barometric pressure sensor circuit. Signal missing, implausible, or wiring broken. Generic fault when no more specific MAP code applies.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor cracked or disconnected

records.titleEn: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor signal is implausible relative to throttle position and engine speed. The ECU expects MAP to rise with throttle opening and fall under deceleration; deviation triggers the code.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor cracked or detached

records.titleEn: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The MAP sensor reports a pressure below the lower threshold the ECU expects at any engine state. Typically indicates a hard electrical fault rather than a slow drift.

records.titleEn: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor High Input
records.descriptionEn: The MAP sensor reports a pressure above the upper threshold the ECU expects in any engine state. Typically caused by a short in the signal circuit or a sensor that has failed producing a fixed high output.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

records.titleEn: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the MAP/BARO sensor circuit. Fault is not constantly present — typically caused by loose connectors, chafed wiring, or a sensor failing under thermal load.

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Generic electrical fault on MAF sensor B (second sensor for redundancy or twin-intake systems).

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: MAF sensor B reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: MAF B signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: MAF B signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from MAF sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation
records.descriptionEn: MAF sensor A and B disagree beyond plausible deviation. One is reading incorrectly.

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general electrical fault in the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor circuit. Signal absent, shorted or out of plausible range. Generic catch-all when no more specific IAT code (low/high/range) is set.

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor reading does not change plausibly with engine warm-up or after driving begins. Many vehicles share the IAT into the MAF housing; on those, MAF replacement also replaces IAT.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element coated with oil or dirt
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The IAT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot intake (low NTC resistance). Usually a wiring short to ground or a failed sensor.

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input
records.descriptionEn: The IAT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold intake (open-circuit-like behaviour). Usually open wiring or a sensor that has failed open.

causes.labelEn: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The IAT signal shows intermittent dropouts or jumps that fall outside slope expectations but do not stay above or below threshold long enough to trigger P0112/P0113. Usually a wiring or connector issue.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general fault has been detected in the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. The ECU uses ECT for fuel enrichment during cold start, fan control, and closed-loop entry timing.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The coolant temperature sensor reading does not change plausibly during warm-up, or its value disagrees with the intake air temperature when the engine has been off long enough that they should match. Often caused by a sensor that reports near a fixed value despite engine warm-up.

causes.labelEn: Thermostat stuck open (engine never reaches operating temperature)
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The ECT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot coolant temperature (typical NTC sensor characteristic — low resistance at high temperature).
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor High Input
records.descriptionEn: The ECT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold temperature (open-circuit-like behaviour). When this code is active, the ECU runs a default cold-start enrichment that wastes fuel and may cause black smoke.

causes.labelEn: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. Fault not constantly present, typically due to loose connector, chafed wiring or a sensor failing thermally.

causes.labelEn: Wiring chafed near hot engine parts

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
records.descriptionEn: ECT sensors 1 and 2 readings disagree beyond plausible limits — typically near startup both should match within tolerance.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation
records.descriptionEn: ECT and IAT readings disagree at long soak (engine off for hours) when both should match ambient. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 1 disagree at long soak. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

records.titleEn: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 2 disagree at long soak. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Throttle Position Sensor / Switch A Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the throttle position sensor/switch A circuit. Signal missing, implausible, or wiring broken. Generic catch-all when no more specific TPS-A code applies.

causes.labelEn: TPS worn or failed (dead spot in resistive track)
TPS mechanically misaligned to throttle shaft

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The throttle position sensor (TPS) signal does not match the expected range for the commanded pedal position. On drive-by-wire vehicles, two redundant sensors are compared; a divergence between them or implausible motion triggers this code.

causes.labelEn: TPS contact track worn (older potentiometer-type sensors)

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The TPS signal voltage is below the lower acceptable threshold. The ECU usually enters limp-home mode and limits engine torque while the fault is active.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" High Input
records.descriptionEn: The TPS signal voltage exceeds the upper acceptable threshold. As with P0122, limp-home mode is typical until the fault clears.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The TPS signal shows intermittent dropouts that do not stay outside threshold long enough to trigger P0122/P0123. Drive-by-wire systems are sensitive to this and may briefly enter limp-home mode each time.

causes.labelEn: Sensor track worn at one spot (older potentiometer-type)
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control
records.descriptionEn: The engine has run long enough that closed-loop fuel control should be active, but the coolant temperature has not risen high enough. Often caused by a stuck-open thermostat or a failed coolant temperature sensor.

records.titleEn: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
records.descriptionEn: Coolant temperature stays below the value expected for stable engine operation. Almost always points to a thermostat stuck open or a sensor reading lower than the actual engine temperature.

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: Intake air temperature exceeds the safe maximum. Risk of preignition or knock; ECU may reduce power.

records.titleEn: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
records.descriptionEn: The engine has been running long enough to reach operating temperature, but coolant temperature stayed below the thermostat's regulating value. Almost always caused by a thermostat stuck open. Costs fuel economy and increases cold-engine emissions.

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: Barometric pressure reading below the plausible minimum. Either operating at extreme altitude or sensor fault.

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Generic electrical fault on turbo/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A reading implausible. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from turbo inlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature / Engine Oil Temperature Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Engine coolant and oil temperature readings disagree beyond plausible limits. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an implausible signal — typically stuck mid-range, no switching between rich and lean, or no signal at all. Closed-loop fuel control cannot run while this fault is active.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage, indicating the ECU sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 1 — or the sensor signal path is shorted to ground.

causes.labelEn: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
Genuine lean running (vacuum leak, low fuel pressure)

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich exhaust on bank 1 or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.

causes.labelEn: Genuine rich running (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor poisoned by silicone or coolant

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor switches between rich and lean too slowly. Aged sensors lose response speed before they fail outright; this code typically appears before P0130/P0131/P0132.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects that the upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 shows no switching activity or responds too slowly to changing exhaust gas composition. Often the sensor is aged, contaminated by silicone or fuel additives, or the heater circuit is degraded.

causes.labelEn: Sensor aged or poisoned (silicone, lead, coolant)
Exhaust leak upstream of sensor diluting reading

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The heating element inside the upstream oxygen sensor draws no current, draws too much current, or is open-circuit. The heater brings the sensor to operating temperature so closed-loop control can start within seconds rather than minutes.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: A general fault has been detected in the downstream (post-catalyst) oxygen sensor on bank 1. The downstream sensor monitors catalyst efficiency rather than fuel mixture; with no signal, the catalyst monitor cannot run.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage. Either the catalyst is letting unburned oxygen through (sensor sees lean), the sensor itself is shorted to ground, or the catalyst is so degraded that the downstream signal mirrors a lean upstream condition.

causes.labelEn: Exhaust leak between catalyst and downstream sensor

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich downstream reading (less common, since post-cat exhaust should be more stable) or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects that the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an abnormally high voltage signal, suggesting a persistently rich exhaust condition past the catalyst, a shorted sensor, or wiring shorted to a voltage source.

causes.labelEn: Engine running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Sensor signal wire shorted to voltage

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. Sensor aging or contamination.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. Sensor aging or contamination.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects no switching or excessively slow response from the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1. Typical for an aged or poisoned sensor; downstream sensors should show a relatively flat signal but must respond to fueling changes during diagnostic monitor runs.

causes.labelEn: Catalytic converter so degraded that downstream signal mirrors upstream

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The heating element inside the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 is open-circuit, drawing no current, or drawing too much. Without heater, the sensor takes much longer to reach operating temperature, delaying catalyst diagnosis.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1. The heater current is out of range, suggesting an open or shorted heater element, blown fuse or wiring fault.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third oxygen sensor in the bank 1 exhaust path (typically located after a second catalyst on diesel or large engines with multi-cat exhausts).

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Indicates persistently lean exhaust, an open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.

causes.labelEn: Lean exhaust (vacuum leak, low fuel pressure)

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Indicates persistently rich exhaust, a shorted sensor or wiring shorted to a voltage source.

causes.labelEn: Rich exhaust (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Typical for aged or poisoned sensor.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Heater current out of range, indicating open/shorted heater element, blown fuse or wiring fault.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: Fuel Delivery Error
records.descriptionEn: Fuel quantity actually delivered does not match the commanded value over a long observation window. Mechanical issue in the fuel system.

records.titleEn: Fuel Timing Error
records.descriptionEn: Injection timing deviates from target. Often caused by chain wear, sensor offset, or injector response drift.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0130 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine. Closed-loop fuel control on bank 2 is disabled while this fault is active.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0131 but on bank 2. The upstream sensor sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 2 or has a signal short to ground.

causes.labelEn: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
Bank 2 running lean (vacuum leak, fuel pressure)
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0132 but on bank 2. The upstream sensor reports a continuously rich condition or has a short to supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Bank 2 running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently rich exhaust, shorted sensor or wiring shorted to voltage.

causes.labelEn: Bank 2 running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Typically aged or poisoned sensor, weak heater, or upstream exhaust leak.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0135 but on the upstream sensor of bank 2. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0136 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2. The catalyst efficiency monitor for bank 2 cannot run while this fault is active.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently lean exhaust past the catalyst, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 (alternate definition mapping in some manufacturers' interpretation). Indicates persistent lean reading, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently rich exhaust past the cat, shorted sensor or wiring shorted to voltage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Fuel Timing Control
records.descriptionEn: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop control of fuel injection timing. Often slow sensor warm-up.

records.titleEn: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Cylinder Balance Control
records.descriptionEn: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop cylinder balance control.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Often aged or poisoned sensor; downstream sensors usually flat but must respond on diagnostic monitor runs.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0141 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Heater current out of range — open or shorted heater element, blown fuse, or wiring fault.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third O2 sensor in the bank 2 exhaust path (typically post-second-cat in multi-cat exhausts).

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates lean exhaust, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates rich exhaust or wiring shorted to voltage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Typically aged or poisoned sensor or weak heater.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Heater current out of range — open or shorted heater, blown fuse, wiring fault.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: Fuel temperature exceeds the safe maximum. Risk of fuel pump damage and injection imprecision.

records.titleEn: Incorrect Fuel Composition
records.descriptionEn: Fuel composition (e.g. ethanol fraction on flex-fuel vehicles) outside expected range. Wrong fuel filled or sensor fault.

causes.labelEn: Wrong fuel filled (e.g. E85 in non-flex)

records.titleEn: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control
records.descriptionEn: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop air/fuel ratio control. Most often O2 sensor heater aging or coolant temperature reading wrong.

records.titleEn: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Rich
records.descriptionEn: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its lean correction limit because mixture is structurally too rich. Likely fuel pressure too high, leaking injector, or O2 sensor reporting too lean.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Lean
records.descriptionEn: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its rich correction limit because mixture is structurally too lean. Likely vacuum leak, low fuel pressure, or contaminated MAF.

records.titleEn: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control
records.descriptionEn: ECU took longer than allowed to close the loop on fuel pressure control. Pressure rise too slow at start.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its lower limit because rail pressure is structurally too high.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its upper limit because rail pressure is structurally too low.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Trim Malfunction (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects that short-term and long-term fuel trim values on bank 1 are outside acceptable limits. Engine cannot maintain stoichiometric mixture — typically a vacuum leak, fuel pressure issue, or failing MAF/O2 sensor.

causes.labelEn: Fuel pressure too low or too high

records.titleEn: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Long-term fuel trim on bank 1 is at the upper limit — the ECU is adding more fuel than baseline to maintain stoichiometric mixture but cannot reach target. Indicates unmetered air entering the intake or insufficient fuel delivery.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum leak in intake or PCV system

records.titleEn: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Long-term fuel trim on bank 1 is at the lower limit — the ECU is removing fuel from baseline but mixture remains too rich. Indicates excess fuel delivery, restricted air flow, or a faulty oxygen sensor reporting falsely lean.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Trim Malfunction Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trims on bank 2 exceed adaptation limits in either lean or rich direction. The ECU cannot maintain stoichiometric mixture within calibrated boundaries.

records.titleEn: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0171 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine (V6, V8, flat-six, etc.). When P0171 and P0174 appear together, the cause is usually a shared component such as the MAF sensor or a central vacuum leak rather than a bank-specific fault.

causes.labelEn: Central vacuum leak (intake manifold gasket, brake booster)

records.titleEn: System Too Rich (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P0172 but on bank 2. When paired with P0172, suspect shared causes (fuel pressure, blocked air filter); when alone, suspect a bank-specific injector or oxygen sensor.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the flex-fuel composition sensor circuit. The sensor measures ethanol content (E0–E85) in the fuel; signal missing, shorted or out of plausible range.

records.titleEn: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range / Performance
records.descriptionEn: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not match expected values for the current fuel mix or rate-of-change is implausible.

records.titleEn: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal is below the minimum threshold. Likely shorted to ground, open circuit or failed sensor.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal exceeds the maximum threshold. Likely shorted to voltage, open ground or failed sensor.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Generic electrical fault on cylinder head temperature sensor A (CHT sensor — used on engines without conventional ECT).

records.titleEn: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: CHT sensor A reading implausible.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: CHT sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: CHT sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from CHT sensor A. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Module Air Filter Restricted
records.descriptionEn: Air filter on the EVAP leak detection pump module is restricted. Leak detection cannot establish reference pressure.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor A circuit. Fuel temperature input is missing or out of plausible range — typical for sensor failure or wiring open/short.

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range / Performance
records.descriptionEn: The fuel temperature sensor A signal is within electrical limits but inconsistent with plausibility checks (e.g. doesn't change with engine warmup, disagrees with ambient temperature).

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The fuel temperature sensor A signal is below the minimum threshold. Likely shorted to ground or open circuit.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: The fuel temperature sensor A signal exceeds the maximum threshold. Likely shorted to voltage, open ground or sensor open-circuit.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the fuel temperature sensor A circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing thermally.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor B circuit (second sensor used on systems with separate supply/return temperature monitoring or twin-tank arrangements).

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range / Performance
records.descriptionEn: Fuel temperature sensor B reading is within electrical limits but implausible (no warmup change, disagrees with sensor A or ambient).

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: Fuel temperature sensor B signal below minimum. Shorted to ground or sensor open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: Fuel temperature sensor B signal exceeds maximum. Shorted to voltage, open ground or open sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the fuel temperature sensor B circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing under thermal load.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load

records.titleEn: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Frequent Activation
records.descriptionEn: The mechanical pressure relief valve has activated repeatedly within a short window — pressure regulation is failing more than once.

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an out-of-range signal from the fuel rail pressure sensor. The voltage is outside calibrated min/max boundaries during normal operation.

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Range / Performance
records.descriptionEn: The fuel rail pressure sensor signal is within electrical limits but doesn't match commanded rail pressure under various engine loads. Common in common-rail diesel and GDI petrol engines.

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The ECU reads a voltage from the fuel rail pressure sensor below the calibrated minimum, indicating short to ground or open supply.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High Input

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Generic electrical fault on engine coolant temperature sensor 3 (third measurement location, e.g. radiator outlet or heater core).
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: ECT sensor 3 reading implausible. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: ECT sensor 3 signal voltage above expected range. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Generic electrical fault on the bank 1, sensor 4 oxygen sensor (fourth sensor downstream — used on systems with multiple cat stages or NOx-trap diagnosis).

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor signal voltage below expected range — short to ground or sensor stuck low.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor signal voltage above expected range — short to power or sensor stuck high. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor responds too slowly to mixture changes. Sensor aged. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor shows no signal change despite operating conditions that should produce activity. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor signal is biased low — sensor stuck reading lean regardless of true mixture. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor signal is biased high — sensor stuck reading rich regardless of true mixture. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Heater A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High

causes.labelEn: Short circuit in heater wiring or element

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all

Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Cold Start Injector 1
records.descriptionEn: Fault detected on cold start injector 1 (auxiliary injector for cold engine starting on some older systems). A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

records.titleEn: Cold Start Injector 2
records.descriptionEn: Fault detected on cold start injector 2. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

records.titleEn: Engine Shutoff Solenoid

records.titleEn: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
records.descriptionEn: Coolant temperature exceeded the safe maximum. Engine overheating event detected — risk of head gasket damage or seizure.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Transmission Fluid Over Temperature
records.descriptionEn: The TCM/PCM detected that automatic transmission fluid temperature exceeded the safe operating threshold. Continued operation accelerates wear on clutches and friction surfaces; many vehicles will engage a fail-safe mode and limit gear selection.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Engine Overspeed Condition
records.descriptionEn: The ECU recorded an engine speed above the manufacturer's redline limit. Typical causes are missed downshifts, mis-shifts on a manual gearbox, or runaway diesel events. The code is informational but may trigger fuel cut-off and protective derate.

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault was detected in the secondary (B) throttle or pedal position sensor circuit. Modern drive-by-wire systems use redundant TPS tracks; the ECU compares them and flags this code on the B channel when out of range.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The B channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor reports values that do not correlate with the A channel or with engine load. Often caused by mechanical wear in the resistive track or by a sticking pedal/throttle plate.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The B channel voltage is below the lower diagnostic threshold, suggesting an open circuit, short to ground, or sensor element failure on track B.

causes.labelEn: TPS B circuit open or shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: The B channel voltage is above the upper diagnostic threshold, typically caused by a short to supply voltage or a defective sensor.

causes.labelEn: TPS B circuit shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Intermittent signal from throttle position sensor B (electronic throttle systems use redundant sensors).

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: CAC cooling fan control voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit High

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit Driver Performance
records.descriptionEn: Driver stage of CAC cooling fan control reports performance fault.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 10 Contribution/Balance
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 10 contributes less power than expected.

causes.labelEn: Injector or ignition coil weak on cylinder 10

records.titleEn: Cylinder 11 Injector A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 11 injector A control voltage below expected range. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Vehicle Overspeed Condition
records.descriptionEn: Vehicle speed exceeded a defined safety threshold. ECU may trigger fuel cut or speed limiter.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Over Temperature
records.descriptionEn: Engine oil temperature exceeded the safe maximum. Risk of oil breakdown and bearing damage.

causes.labelEn: Oil cooler failure or low oil level

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger "A" Underboost Condition
records.descriptionEn: Boost pressure under load is below the commanded value. Very common on turbodiesel and direct-injection turbo gasoline engines as the turbo system ages — typically a leaking boost pipe, a sticky variable-geometry vane assembly, or a wastegate that no longer holds.

causes.labelEn: Leak in intercooler pipe or hose
Wastegate stuck open or weak spring
Turbo bearing worn (preceded by oil consumption / smoke)

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Overboost Condition
records.descriptionEn: Boost pressure on the secondary turbocharger/supercharger (B) on a sequential or twin-charged setup is above the upper threshold. Wastegate stuck closed, VGT vanes stuck, or boost pressure sensor reads high.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Underboost Condition
records.descriptionEn: Boost pressure on the secondary turbocharger/supercharger (B) is below the lower threshold. Wastegate stuck open, charge-air leak, or VGT vanes stuck open.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
records.descriptionEn: The PCM applies a per-cylinder injector offset (Mengenausgleich) to compensate for production-tolerance differences in injector flow rate. On cylinder 1 the learned correction has reached its minimum value — the injector is delivering significantly more fuel than the calibrated reference and the controller cannot trim it any further.

causes.labelEn: Injector over-delivering — worn nozzle or stuck-open seat
Calibration code not programmed after replacement

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
records.descriptionEn: The per-cylinder injector offset on cylinder 1 has reached its maximum value — the injector is delivering significantly less fuel than the calibrated reference, and the controller cannot trim it any further.

causes.labelEn: Injector under-delivering — clogged nozzle or worn coil
Calibration code not programmed after replacement

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit for the diesel intake air-flow control valve A is open. This valve (also called intake throttle, swirl flap actuator, or anti-shudder valve) closes the diesel intake to control airflow during regeneration and shutdown.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Performance
records.descriptionEn: Diesel intake air-flow control A is electrically OK but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically carbon buildup or seized actuator.

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Diesel intake air-flow control A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Diesel intake air-flow control A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: Diesel intake throttle A is mechanically stuck open — anti-shudder function on shutdown will not work and DPF regen airflow control is lost.

causes.labelEn: Carbon buildup or broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Diesel intake throttle A is mechanically stuck closed — engine starves of intake air.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on diesel intake throttle A position sensor — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Position sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails — does not match commanded throttle position.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Motor Current Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Motor current draw of the diesel intake throttle A actuator does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction from carbon.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected
records.descriptionEn: Air flow through diesel intake throttle A is higher than the commanded set point — flap leaking past the seat or stuck partly open.

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
records.descriptionEn: Air flow through diesel intake throttle A is lower than the commanded set point — flap stuck partly closed.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The cylinder 1 injector drive circuit is electrically OK but the response (current ramp, dwell time, or peak voltage) does not match the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or wiring corrosion.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Injector Circuit Range/Performance

records.titleEn: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: The diesel intake throttle position sensor does not reach the calibrated minimum or maximum stop value during a self-test sweep — typically sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a sticky throttle plate.

records.titleEn: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit for the cold-start auxiliary fuel injector or the cold-start ECU output is open. Some diesels use an extra cold-start injector to inject fuel into the intake manifold during very cold starts.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Cold-start injector drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit High

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Cold-start injector drive is electrically OK but does not deliver the calibrated injection quantity — partial blockage or weak coil.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Propulsion System Inactive Timer Performance
records.descriptionEn: The timer that monitors how long the propulsion system has been inactive (used by hybrid and stop-start strategies to schedule rebalancing tasks) is not behaving plausibly — typically a clock or PCM-state fault.

records.titleEn: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
records.descriptionEn: The ECU has detected misfires that are not concentrated on a single cylinder. The misfire monitor measures crankshaft acceleration after each combustion event; missing acceleration on multiple cylinders, or randomly across cylinders, triggers this code.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
records.descriptionEn: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 1. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.

causes.labelEn: Spark plug for cylinder 1 worn or fouled

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
records.descriptionEn: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 2. Diagnostic approach is identical to P0301 — swap the suspect coil or plug with a known-good cylinder and see if the misfire follows.

causes.labelEn: Spark plug for cylinder 2 worn or fouled

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
records.descriptionEn: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 3. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. Verify by swapping the suspected coil/plug to a different cylinder; if the code follows, the part is bad.

causes.labelEn: Spark plug for cylinder 3 worn or fouled

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
records.descriptionEn: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 4. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. Verify by swapping the suspected coil/plug to a different cylinder; if the code follows, the part is bad.

causes.labelEn: Spark plug for cylinder 4 worn or fouled

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected
records.descriptionEn: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 5 (only present on engines with 5+ cylinders). Same diagnostic approach as P0301 — swap the suspect coil/plug with another cylinder.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open: the circuit is open. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.

causes.labelEn: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The ignition B control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.

causes.labelEn: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Ignition B control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Ignition B control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
