symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Misfire Detected with Low Fuel
records.descriptionEn: Misfires are detected while the fuel level is low. The ECM disables further misfire reporting under this condition because intermittent fuel starvation can cause false positives in catalyst-damaging logic.
symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Single Cylinder Misfire — Cylinder Not Specified
records.descriptionEn: A persistent misfire is detected on one cylinder, but the engine controller cannot identify which cylinder is affected. Often seen on engines without per-cylinder feedback or when crank position correlation fails.

causes.labelEn: Weak ignition component on one cylinder

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position System Variation Not Learned
records.descriptionEn: The PCM has not yet learned the crankshaft position variation table required for accurate misfire detection. After flywheel/sensor replacement or PCM relearn, a procedure must be performed (typically deceleration from a defined RPM with closed throttle).

records.titleEn: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
records.descriptionEn: The misfire monitor detected misfires during the first 1000 revolutions after startup but the engine then settled. Often caused by fouled spark plugs that warm up clean, weak ignition coils, or a borderline cold-start fuel mixture.

causes.labelEn: Ignition coil weak below operating temperature
Cold-start mixture too lean (fuel pressure, leaking injectors at rest)

symptomsEn: Check engine light on or flashing
Possible smell of unburned fuel from exhaust

records.titleEn: Rough Road Hardware Not Present
records.descriptionEn: The PCM has been configured to use rough-road sensor input for misfire detection (to mask false positives on bumpy surfaces) but the expected hardware is not detected on the network. Typically a configuration mismatch after replacement.

causes.labelEn: PCM configuration does not match installed hardware

records.titleEn: Rough Road Sensor A Signal Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on rough-road sensor A — used to gate misfire detection so that engine vibration from rough roads is not misclassified as misfire.

records.titleEn: Rough Road Sensor B Signal Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on rough-road sensor B — used to gate misfire detection so that engine vibration from rough roads is not misclassified as misfire.

records.titleEn: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The ignition C control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.

causes.labelEn: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Ignition C control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Ignition C control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The ignition D control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.

causes.labelEn: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Ignition D control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Ignition D control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on the engine speed input from the ignition/distributor — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. On older systems this is the distributor pickup; on newer ones it is the crank/cam-derived speed signal feeding the ignition driver.

records.titleEn: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Engine speed input from the ignition/distributor is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — slow response, drift, or noise.

causes.labelEn: Sensor drift or pickup gap wrong
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
records.descriptionEn: No engine speed signal from the ignition/distributor — open circuit, dead pickup, or sensor air gap too wide.

causes.labelEn: Pickup dead or air gap excessive

records.titleEn: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Engine speed input signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or wiring issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Control System Error
records.descriptionEn: The knock-control subsystem reports an internal error — typically a self-test fault or a noise floor that cannot be calibrated. The system protects against detonation by retarding ignition; with this fault knock control is disabled.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: A general fault has been detected in the bank 1 knock sensor circuit. The ECU uses the knock sensor to detect pre-ignition and retards ignition timing when knock occurs; with no signal, the ECU runs conservative timing and loses power.

causes.labelEn: Sensor mounting bolt loose (sensor must be torqued correctly)

symptomsEn: Power loss from defensive spark retard

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor A signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

records.titleEn: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The knock sensor signal voltage is below the expected range. Usually points to a piezoelectric sensor that has lost its output, or a short to ground in the signal line.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Power loss from defensive spark retard

records.titleEn: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit High Input (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The knock sensor signal voltage is above the expected range. Often caused by a sensor producing excess output due to mechanical noise (loose mounting, accessory drive vibration) rather than a sensor fault.

causes.labelEn: Mechanical noise picked up by sensor (loose accessory)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

symptomsEn: Power loss from defensive spark retard

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on knock sensor C — used on engines with multiple knock sensors (one per bank or per cylinder pair).

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor C signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor C signal below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor C signal above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Combustion Engine Producing Insufficient Torque
records.descriptionEn: The engine torque measured (or modelled from intake/exhaust signals) is below the calibrated set point for the commanded throttle position. Causes range from low compression, intake leak, fuel pressure issue, ignition fault, to high mechanical drag.

causes.labelEn: Low compression on one or more cylinders

records.titleEn: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault in the bank 2 knock sensor circuit. The ECU monitors a piezoelectric sensor for engine vibration patterns associated with detonation; an open, shorted, or out-of-range circuit triggers this code.
symptomsEn: Power loss from defensive spark retard

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor B signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit Low Input (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor 2 (bank 2) reports a signal level below the diagnostic threshold. The sensor is a piezo element bolted to the engine block; output should be a small AC voltage on each combustion event. A cold or open sensor reads 0 V; a loose mounting bolt damps the signal. Without knock detection, the ECM retards spark globally as a safety measure — fuel economy and power suffer.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Power loss from defensive spark retard

records.titleEn: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit High Input (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The bank 2 knock sensor signal is above the expected voltage range. Typically caused by a short to supply voltage or an internal sensor fault.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Power loss from defensive spark retard

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor signal is missing or implausible. The CKP is essential — without it the ECU cannot synchronise injection or ignition, and the engine will not start or will stall.

causes.labelEn: Reluctor ring damaged or contaminated with metal debris

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The CKP signal is present but inconsistent with engine RPM, or pulse counts deviate from the reluctor's expected pattern. Often points to a damaged tooth on the reluctor or an air gap that has changed.

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The CKP signal voltage is below the lower threshold. Usually a sensor whose internal coil has degraded, or a wiring short to ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: The CKP signal voltage is above the upper threshold. Either a sensor producing excess output or a short to supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The crankshaft position sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector, sensor air gap, or damaged tone wheel. The PCM may detect a "false" stall or misfire spike when the signal drops.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on knock sensor D — used on engines with multiple knock sensors (one per bank or per cylinder pair).

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor D signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor D signal below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor D signal above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Knock sensor D signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

records.titleEn: Crankshaft/Camshaft Loss Of Synchronization
records.descriptionEn: The PCM has lost crank-to-cam synchronization — the relative phase between crankshaft and camshaft no longer matches the calibrated reference. Causes include a stretched or jumped timing chain, broken cam timing tooth, or sensor signal corruption.

causes.labelEn: Crank or cam sensor signal corrupted

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
records.descriptionEn: The camshaft position (CMP) sensor signal is missing or implausible. The ECU uses CMP together with CKP to identify cylinder phase for sequential injection and coil-on-plug ignition; without CMP the engine may run on group injection or fail to start.

causes.labelEn: Timing chain stretched, throwing off sensor timing

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The CMP signal is present but its phase relative to the crankshaft is outside tolerance. On engines with variable valve timing, this code often appears together with VVT solenoid faults.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The CMP signal voltage is below the lower threshold. Most often a sensor with degraded internal output or a short to ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit High Input (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The CMP signal voltage is above the upper threshold. Either excessive sensor output or a short to supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
records.descriptionEn: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 or Single Sensor): the signal is intermittent or erratic. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault in the bank 2 camshaft position sensor circuit. The ECU uses this signal together with the crank sensor for sequential injection and ignition timing.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The bank 2 camshaft position sensor signal is present but does not match the crank reference correctly, or its pulse pattern is implausible.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Camshaft position sensor A on bank 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Camshaft position sensor A on bank 2 reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Start Position Incorrect
records.descriptionEn: At engine start the crankshaft position reported by the sensor does not match the calibrated start window — typically a wrong tone-wheel installation, sensor air gap, or PCM not synchronised after a relearn.

causes.labelEn: Tone wheel misindexed or relearn pending

records.titleEn: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Direction Incorrect
records.descriptionEn: The crankshaft is rotating in the wrong direction relative to the expected reference — typically only seen on stop-start systems where the engine briefly counter-rotates after shutdown.

records.titleEn: Ion Sense System Performance
records.descriptionEn: Some engines (notably Saab and some Mazda direct-injection units) use the spark plug as an ion-current sensor after spark to detect knock and misfire. This code reports a performance issue with the ion-sense input — typically a worn plug, loose secondary connection, or aged ion-sense module.

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: A general open-circuit fault has been detected on an ignition coil's primary or secondary winding (no specific cylinder identified). This code is set when the PCM cannot localise the fault to a single coil.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil "A" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 1)
records.descriptionEn: An electrical fault is detected in both the primary and the secondary circuit of ignition coil A (cylinder 1). The ECU cannot drive the coil correctly, so the cylinder served by coil A misfires or does not fire at all. records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Pressure Variation High

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Combustion Performance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general fault has been detected in the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system. EGR routes a portion of exhaust back into the intake to reduce combustion temperature and NOx emissions. Most EGR codes today are caused by carbon buildup blocking the valve.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected
records.descriptionEn: When the ECU commands EGR open, the actual flow measured by the DPFE sensor or the resulting MAP/MAF change is below threshold. By far the most common cause is a carboned-up EGR valve or blocked intake passages.

causes.labelEn: EGR valve clogged or stuck closed
Intake EGR passages blocked with carbon
Vacuum line to EGR (vacuum-actuated valves) cracked

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected
records.descriptionEn: EGR flow is higher than expected when the valve should be closed, or higher than commanded when partially open. Typically a valve that has stuck open due to carbon, causing rough idle and stalling.

causes.labelEn: Valve seat eroded — does not seal

records.titleEn: EGR Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit for the EGR valve solenoid is open or shorted. The ECM cannot drive the valve to the commanded position.

records.titleEn: EGR Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The EGR valve does not move through its expected range or its position feedback does not track command. The valve may be sticking, the position sensor may be drifting or carbon buildup is preventing full travel.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The signal from EGR position or pressure sensor B is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates a short to ground, open signal wire or sensor fault.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on EGR temperature sensor A — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor monitors recirculated exhaust gas temperature for EGR cooler protection and dosing.

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor A below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor A above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general fault in the secondary air injection system. The system pumps fresh air into the exhaust during cold start to accelerate catalyst light-off; common faults are a seized pump, blocked passages or a stuck valve.

causes.labelEn: Air pump seized (water ingress is a common cause)

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow
records.descriptionEn: When the ECU commands secondary air injection, the actual flow measured by the front oxygen sensor (or a dedicated mass flow meter) does not match the expected value. Usually a partially blocked passage or a leaking combi valve.

causes.labelEn: Air passages in cylinder head clogged with carbon

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Open: the circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed component.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit Shorted
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detected a short circuit in the secondary air injection switching valve A control circuit. With the valve unable to switch correctly, the cold-start emissions strategy fails and the catalyst takes longer to reach light-off.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Open: the circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed component.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit Shorted
records.descriptionEn: AIR switching valve B drive circuit shorted to ground or B+.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Relay "A" Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault in the secondary air injection pump relay A circuit. Without the relay, the air pump cannot be commanded and the system cannot complete its cold-start function.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on AIR system control circuit B (typically the AIR pump driver line on the second pump or relay).

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on EGR temperature sensor B — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor monitors recirculated exhaust gas temperature for EGR cooler protection and dosing.

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor B below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor B above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: EGR temperature sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: AIR switching valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The oxygen storage capacity of the main catalytic converter on bank 1 has degraded below the OBD threshold. The downstream oxygen sensor signal increasingly mirrors the upstream sensor, indicating reduced conversion efficiency.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The pre-cat (warm-up) catalyst on bank 1 has lost too much oxygen storage capacity. Its primary purpose — quickly reaching light-off after a cold start — is no longer met within the OBD limits.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Main Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Generic main catalyst efficiency code on bank 1 — used by some manufacturers in addition to or instead of P0420. Indicates the same root cause — degraded oxygen storage in the main catalyst.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Heated Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Heated (electrically warmed) catalyst on bank 1 fails efficiency monitoring. In addition to standard catalyst aging, faults in the catalyst heater control or supply can cause this code.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Heated Catalyst Temperature Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The heated catalyst on bank 1 does not reach its target temperature within the expected time. Common causes are a defective heater element, supply fault, or a damaged temperature sensor.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault detected in the catalyst temperature sensor on bank 1 sensor position 1. The ECU uses this signal to manage heater control and protect the catalyst from overtemperature.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit for the heated catalyst on bank 1 is open. Heated catalysts use an electrical heating element to reach light-off temperature within seconds of cold start.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the catalyst temperature sensor at bank 1 sensor 2.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

records.titleEn: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
records.descriptionEn: During the EVAP leak-detection self-test, the calibration airflow through the reference orifice is below the expected rate. The orifice may be partially blocked.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice High Flow
records.descriptionEn: During the leak-detection self-test, airflow through the reference orifice is above the expected rate — typically a leak around the orifice or a damaged seal.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general fault in the evaporative emission (EVAP) system has been detected. The system seals the fuel tank and captures fuel vapour in a charcoal canister; this code indicates a failed leak test or sensor without identifying the specific failure.

causes.labelEn: Fuel filler cap loose or worn
Purge valve stuck open or closed

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
records.descriptionEn: The actual purge flow does not match the commanded value. Usually a purge valve stuck closed (no flow) or stuck open (too much flow at idle). Distinct from a leak code.

causes.labelEn: Purge valve stuck open or closed

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
records.descriptionEn: A small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.040 inch / 1.0 mm orifice) has been detected in the EVAP system. By far the most common cause is a fuel cap that is loose, missing, or has a worn seal.

causes.labelEn: Fuel cap loose, missing, or worn seal

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Electrical fault in the EVAP purge solenoid circuit. The ECU detects an open, shorted, or out-of-range condition on the purge valve driver.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The ECU has detected an open circuit in the purge solenoid control line — usually a broken wire, unplugged connector, or open coil winding.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detected a short in the EVAP purge solenoid control circuit. With the valve permanently energized or shorted, the system can either over-purge causing rich running, or stay closed.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission Vent Control Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A fault in the EVAP vent valve circuit. The vent valve seals the canister against atmosphere during the leak test; without it, the test cannot pull a vacuum and may set false leak codes alongside.

causes.labelEn: Vent valve seized or contaminated by water/dirt

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detected an open circuit on the EVAP vent valve control. The vent valve is needed to seal the system for leak diagnostics; with the circuit open the leak test cannot complete.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
records.descriptionEn: EVAP vent valve drive circuit shorted to ground or B+. The vent valve seals the canister during pressure-test diagnostics.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault was detected in the EVAP vent valve/solenoid control circuit. Without a working vent valve the EVAP leak test cannot complete and the system may remain not-ready.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit
records.descriptionEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: EGR sensor C below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: EGR sensor C above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: EGR sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: AIR switching valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on EVAP pressure sensor/switch A — used to monitor canister pressure during leak-detection diagnostics.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The fuel tank pressure sensor reading is implausible — for example, fluctuating signal, noise, or values that do not respond to known pressure events such as a key-on tank refill.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Low Input
records.descriptionEn: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum voltage. Often caused by a failed sensor or a short to ground in the signal line.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor High Input
records.descriptionEn: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is above the expected maximum voltage, typical of a short to supply or a sensor that has failed high.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: EVAP pressure sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
records.descriptionEn: A large leak has been detected during the EVAP system pressure or vacuum test — large enough that the system cannot hold pressure for the diagnostic interval. Typically a missing fuel cap, disconnected hose, or split canister.

causes.labelEn: Fuel cap missing or not seated

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
records.descriptionEn: A very small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.020 inch / 0.5 mm orifice) has been detected. Smaller threshold than P0442; intermittent and often weather-dependent. Modern OBD-II requires this monitor on most vehicles since model year 2000.

causes.labelEn: Fuel cap seal hardened or worn
Purge or vent valve leaking slightly

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Fuel Cap Loose/Off)
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP system detected a large leak that strongly correlates with a missing or improperly closed fuel filler cap. After re-tightening the cap, the code clears once the readiness monitor completes.

causes.labelEn: Fuel cap loose, missing, or worn seal

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: EVAP purge control valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: EVAP purge control valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EGR B Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on EGR control circuit B — second EGR valve on engines with high-pressure and low-pressure EGR loops.

records.titleEn: EGR B Control Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: EGR valve B is electrically OK but does not respond as commanded — typically carbon buildup or sticking actuator.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

Supply wire pinched against B+ source

Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the primary fuel-level sensor (A) — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

records.titleEn: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Fuel-level sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, jumps, or does not match consumption.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Fuel-level sensor A below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Fuel-level sensor A above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

records.titleEn: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit

records.titleEn: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. Reduced cooling-fan control can let the engine or A/C condenser overheat.

records.titleEn: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. Reduced cooling-fan control can let the engine or A/C condenser overheat.

records.titleEn: Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: Electrical fault detected in the third cooling fan control circuit. With one stage of cooling lost, engine and A/C condenser cooling capacity is reduced, particularly at low vehicle speeds.

records.titleEn: Cooling Fan Rationality Check
records.descriptionEn: The ECM detects that the cooling fan response does not match command. Either the fan rotates without command, fails to rotate when commanded or its current draw is implausible.

records.titleEn: Cooling Fan Current Too High
records.descriptionEn: The current draw of the cooling fan exceeds the permitted maximum. Caused by a seized or worn fan motor or wiring shorted to ground at high load.

records.titleEn: Cooling Fan Power/Ground Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A fault is detected in the supply or ground path of the cooling fan circuit. Voltage drops or open ground prevent reliable fan operation.

records.titleEn: EGR Sensor B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on EGR sensor B — second EGR sensor on dual-loop or HP/LP EGR systems. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

records.titleEn: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A/Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit of EGR throttle A is open. EGR throttles partially close intake to increase exhaust gas recirculation flow at low loads.

records.titleEn: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: EGR throttle A is electrically OK but does not move as commanded. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: AIR system flow on bank 1 is below threshold during the cold-start self-test — typically a clogged check valve, leaking hose, or weak air pump.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: AIR system flow on bank 2 is below threshold during the cold-start self-test — typically a clogged check valve, leaking hose, or weak air pump.

records.titleEn: Fan Overspeed
records.descriptionEn: Fan Overspeed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.labelEn: Fan relay welded closed - fan runs uncontrolled

records.titleEn: Fan 1 Underspeed
records.descriptionEn: Cooling fan 1 is rotating slower than commanded. The ECU sees the tachometer feedback below the expected window for the requested duty cycle - usually a worn fan motor, a high-resistance harness or feed, or a partially seized impeller.

causes.labelEn: Fan 1 motor worn or brushes degraded

records.titleEn: Fan 1 Overspeed
records.descriptionEn: Fan 1 Overspeed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

records.titleEn: Evaporative Emission System High Purge Flow
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detected EVAP purge flow during a non-purge condition, or higher than commanded purge flow. Typical causes are a stuck-open purge valve or a damaged vent system that draws unmetered air.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Low Purge Flow
records.descriptionEn: The evaporative emissions system measures purge flow either via a dedicated purge flow sensor or via short-term fuel trim response when the purge valve opens. The flow is significantly lower than expected for the commanded purge rate - typically a clogged purge line, a stuck purge valve, or a leaking vapor canister vent.

causes.labelEn: Purge line restricted by debris or kinks

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The vent valve closes the EVAP canister to atmosphere during leak tests. The control line for that valve is shorted to ground - the ECU drives the valve and measures voltage below the expected level, indicating either a harness short or an internal solenoid short.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0498 with the control line open or shorted to supply. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EGR B Flow
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust-gas recirculation system has a second EGR loop (B) - typically used on engines with a dedicated low-pressure EGR for emissions or on twin-bank V engines. The ECU detects an EGR B flow fault - the measured or modelled flow does not match the requested rate, without yet diagnosing it as too low or too high.

causes.labelEn: EGR valve B sticking due to soot

records.titleEn: EGR B Flow Insufficient Detected
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049A but specifically with measured flow below the required rate - typically EGR valve sticking closed or cooler heavily clogged.

causes.labelEn: EGR cooler B heavily clogged with soot

records.titleEn: EGR B Flow Excessive Detected
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049A but with measured flow above the required rate - typically EGR valve sticking open or position sensor offset low.

records.titleEn: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
records.descriptionEn: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Heavy carbon deposits on EGR A seat

records.titleEn: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
records.descriptionEn: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Heavy carbon deposits on EGR B seat

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the second exhaust pressure control valve (B) - used for example on dual exhaust brakes, twin-bank diesels with separate back-pressure flaps, or for DPF regeneration backpressure assist on the second bank. The ECU loses control of this stage.

causes.labelEn: Open in harness or actuator winding
Connector corroded by exhaust heat or moisture

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049F with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - actuator slow, slipping or position sensor offset.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049F with the control line shorted to ground.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049F with the control line shorted to supply.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049F with intermittent or erratic feedback - typically a connector or harness fault.

causes.labelEn: Intermittent contact at connector or terminal
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust pressure control valve B is mechanically stuck in the open position. The ECU commands closing for back-pressure assist or exhaust braking, but the position feedback shows it remains open - typically heavy soot, broken linkage, or a sticky valve shaft.

causes.labelEn: Valve stuck open due to soot or broken linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04A4 but the valve B is stuck closed - back-pressure stays high even when the engine should run with low restriction; risk of overheating or excessive fuel consumption.

causes.labelEn: Valve stuck closed due to soot or broken linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A circuit fault is detected on the position sensor of exhaust pressure control valve B. Without valid position feedback the ECU cannot run closed-loop control of the valve and falls back to a default substitute.

causes.labelEn: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04A6 with the signal in plausible range but not matching the actual valve angle.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04A6 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The second EVAP purge control valve (B) - used on systems with a divided purge path or on twin-bank engines - shows an open control circuit. The ECU cannot drive the valve, so vapor cannot be purged through this stage; tank pressure may rise and emissions diagnostics fail.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed

records.titleEn: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The refueling vapor control valve - typically part of the ORVR or capless fueling system - has an open control circuit. The valve directs fuel vapor from the tank into the canister during refueling and must open when the fuel filler is opened. Without it, vapor escapes during refueling and the system fails leak diagnostics.

causes.labelEn: Open in harness or solenoid winding
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04B0 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Valve stuck open due to debris or weak spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Stuck Closed

Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
