records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the open-request input - the button or switch the driver presses to release the fuel fill door. The ECU loses the request signal, so motorised release becomes unavailable.

records.titleEn: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Performance Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: The open-request switch never registers an active state - either the contact stays open mechanically or the wiring is permanently broken. The driver cannot trigger door release.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04C8 with the signal voltage shorted to ground or constantly low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04C8 with the signal voltage shorted to supply or constantly high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04C8 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The open-request switch is stuck in the active state - the ECU continuously reads a request to open the fuel fill door. Either the switch is mechanically held closed or the line is shorted to its active level.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit
records.descriptionEn: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04CE with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - typically sensor drift or a slow response after engine warm-up.

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04CE with the signal voltage below the plausible range. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04CE with the signal voltage above the plausible range. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04CE with intermittent or erratic signal. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust brake activation input - typically from a stalk lever, brake pedal switch, or vehicle bus message - shows a circuit fault. The ECU cannot accept a request to engage the exhaust brake, which limits engine braking on heavy vehicles.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D3 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching expected behaviour - e.g. activation request without driver input or no response after a request.

causes.labelEn: Signal implausible against driver action or bus

records.titleEn: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D3 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D3 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D3 with intermittent or erratic signal. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop EGR Control
records.descriptionEn: After cold start the ECU operates EGR open-loop until preconditions (cooler temperature, sensor warm-up, engine load) are met, then transitions into closed-loop control. The transition is taking too long - typically due to a slow EGR temperature sensor, a stuck EGR valve still warming up, or a long-trip drive cycle that does not meet load conditions.

causes.labelEn: Short-trip operation - load conditions not met

records.titleEn: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit Flow Too Low
records.descriptionEn: With EGR running in closed loop the controller has driven the actuator to its maximum opening but cannot reach the required EGR flow. The valve, cooler, or pipework is restricted enough that even full open does not deliver the modelled rate.

causes.labelEn: Valve effective opening reduced by carbon

records.titleEn: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit Flow Too High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D9 with the controller fully closing the actuator yet still measuring more EGR flow than required. The valve does not seat fully, or position feedback under-reads.

causes.labelEn: Valve does not seat fully (debris or wear)

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
records.descriptionEn: A pressure or flow sensor in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) circuit reports atmospheric conditions where it should see crankcase or intake vacuum - the hose between crankcase and intake is disconnected, cracked, or open. PCV no longer routes blow-by gases into the intake, increasing oil mist emissions and risking oil leaks.

causes.labelEn: PCV hose pulled off or split
Oil filler cap missing or loose

records.titleEn: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04B8 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the actuator command - door reports closed when motor commanded open, or vice versa.

causes.labelEn: Sensor signal offset against actual position

records.titleEn: Cold Start EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
records.descriptionEn: During the cold-start strategy the ECU briefly opens EGR A to slow combustion temperatures and reduce engine-out NOx during catalyst light-off. The measured EGR flow stays below the calibrated target despite the requested opening - typically a stuck-closed valve, restricted cold-start path, or sensor offset that under-reports flow.

causes.labelEn: EGR valve A sticking closed when cold

records.titleEn: Cold Start EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04DD with EGR flow above the cold-start target - typically valve sticking open during the cold phase or position sensor offset low.

causes.labelEn: EGR valve A sticking open when cold

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

causes.labelEn: Debris on valve seat prevents full closing
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04AF on EVAP purge valve A. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A dedicated sensor monitors whether the PCV hose is fitted to its connector at the engine. The ECU detects a circuit fault on this sensor - cannot determine whether the hose is connected. Required by some emissions regulations to flag a disconnected PCV hose immediately.

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04E1 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit
records.descriptionEn: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.

causes.labelEn: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04CF on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D0 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D1 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04D2 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP leak diagnostic has detected a small leak on the fuel tank side of the system - typically a hose, gasket, fuel cap, or fuel sender flange that does not seal completely. Vapor escapes during pressure or vacuum tests.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04EA but on the fresh-air side - the path between vent valve and atmosphere is not sealing completely during the active test phase.

causes.labelEn: Vent valve does not seal in test mode

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04EA but the leak is large enough that the system cannot build the test pressure or vacuum at all - typically a missing fuel cap, an unseated hose or a torn vapor line on the tank side.

causes.labelEn: Fuel cap missing or not seated
Vapor hose pulled off or torn

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04EB on the fresh-air side, but with a leak large enough to prevent test build-up. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04EA but at the most sensitive leak threshold - typically the OBD-II 0.020-inch (~0.5 mm) test. The system holds pressure for some time but loses it slower than the diagnostic limit allows; usually fuel cap O-ring fatigue or microcracks in a hose.

causes.labelEn: Fuel cap O-ring aged or stiffened

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04EE on the fresh-air side - microcrack in a hose or imperfect vent valve seal at the most sensitive test threshold.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
records.descriptionEn: On engines that have a separate high-load purge line - to use boost pressure to pull vapor on turbo applications - the ECU monitors flow when this path is commanded. The flow is below the expected level - the venturi, line, or check valve is restricted, or the line is incorrectly routed.

causes.labelEn: Line, venturi or check valve restricted

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Purge Line Performance
records.descriptionEn: A general performance fault on the EVAP purge line - flow does not match the requested rate, without specifying which segment. Usually a partially blocked line, a stuck purge valve, or a leak that decouples flow from valve commands.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The electric catalyst heater on bank 1 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window. The heater cannot deliver the rated power, so cold-start emissions rise until the catalyst reaches light-off conventionally.

causes.labelEn: Heater supply voltage low or unstable
DC/DC converter fault on heater rail

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The electric catalyst heater on bank 2 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window. The heater cannot deliver the rated power, so cold-start emissions rise until the catalyst reaches light-off conventionally.

causes.labelEn: Heater supply voltage low or unstable
DC/DC converter fault on heater rail

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 1 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 2 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04F4 with the line shorted to supply or open - the ECU measures higher voltage than the commanded duty cycle allows.

causes.labelEn: Open in heater element or harness
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04F6 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04F4 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the heater feed.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Same as P04F8 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: EGR A Control Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: The ECU monitors the operating temperature of the EGR A actuator (or its control electronics). The reading has exceeded the safe upper threshold and the control unit derates or disables EGR A to protect the actuator from thermal damage.

causes.labelEn: Actuator overheated due to nearby exhaust heat or duty-cycle stress
Cooling jacket or air flow insufficient

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: The sensor that monitors PCV hose connection reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with the engine model - signal does not switch when the hose is moved during diagnosis, or shows offset against actual hose state.

records.titleEn: Crankcase Ventilation System Performance
records.descriptionEn: A general performance fault of the crankcase ventilation system - PCV pressure or flow does not match the engine model. Possible causes are a clogged PCV valve, blocked separator, oil-filler cap with a damaged seal, or excessive blow-by from worn rings.

causes.labelEn: Excessive blow-by from worn piston rings

records.titleEn: EGR Actuator A Control Processor Performance
records.descriptionEn: Modern smart EGR actuators contain their own microcontroller that handles position control internally and reports back over LIN or PWM. The ECU detects implausible behaviour from the actuator processor - missed messages, incorrect responses, or watchdog resets.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The catalyst heater on bank 1 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated. Heater element ageing, increased contact resistance, or a partial winding failure are typical causes.

causes.labelEn: Heater element aged - reduced power output

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The catalyst heater on bank 2 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated. Heater element ageing, increased contact resistance, or a partial winding failure are typical causes.

causes.labelEn: Heater element aged - reduced power output

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The vehicle speed sensor (VSS) signal is missing or implausible. On automatic transmissions this often disables cruise control and shift adaptation; ABS-equipped cars typically derive speed from wheel speed sensors as a fallback.

records.titleEn: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The VSS signal is present but inconsistent — either values jump implausibly or the sensor reports a speed inconsistent with engine RPM in gear. Often a damaged reluctor ring or a sensor with degraded magnetic response.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The primary vehicle speed sensor (VSS A) reports a signal voltage below the plausible lower limit. With no usable speed signal the ECU loses cruise control, gear-shift logic and certain anti-stall functions.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Erratic or High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0502 with the signal noisy, erratic or above the plausible upper limit - typical for a chafed harness, missing reluctor tooth or a sensor with a weakened magnet.

causes.labelEn: Noise on signal line or intermittent open
Reluctor ring damaged or missing teeth
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Brake Switch "A"/"B" Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Modern vehicles use two redundant brake switch signals (often one normally-open and one normally-closed). When the two signals disagree, this code is set; common causes include a misadjusted switch, internal switch failure, or wiring fault.

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control System Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general fault has been detected in the idle air control (IAC) system. On older vehicles with a separate IAC valve, this means the valve cannot maintain commanded idle RPM; on drive-by-wire systems, the equivalent fault is in the throttle body's idle adaptation.
symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
records.descriptionEn: The engine idles below the target RPM despite the IAC opening fully. Indicates restricted air path past the IAC — typically a heavily fouled throttle body or stuck IAC valve.

causes.labelEn: Throttle body or idle bypass passage clogged

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
records.descriptionEn: Idle RPM exceeds the target despite the IAC commanded fully closed. Almost always caused by a vacuum leak that lets air bypass the IAC — torn intake hose, leaking PCV, brake booster, or intake manifold gasket.
symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The control line to the idle air control valve - which opens a small bypass around the throttle to set idle airflow - is shorted to ground or measures a voltage below the plausible level.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0508 with the line shorted to supply or open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Open in IAC valve or harness
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance
records.descriptionEn: During the cold-start phase the ECU runs an elevated idle speed and a richer mixture to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature quickly. The cold-start idle does not behave as commanded - speed sags, hunts, or fails to come up. Possible causes are intake leaks active when cold, an IAC valve sticking, or implausible coolant temperature.

causes.labelEn: Intake leak only when cold (gasket shrinks)

records.titleEn: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance
records.descriptionEn: During cold-start the ECU retards ignition timing to raise exhaust temperature for catalyst light-off. The strategy does not deliver the expected timing - feedback from knock sensor or combustion model shows ignition too far advanced or retarded for the demanded calibration.

causes.labelEn: Knock sensor drift causes wrong feedback

records.titleEn: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
records.descriptionEn: During cold-start the ECU expects coolant temperature to rise within a calibrated time window. Either the engine warms up too slowly (stuck-open thermostat, weak combustion) or the temperature signal does not reflect the actual warm-up.

causes.labelEn: Thermostat stuck open - engine warms too slowly

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Cold Start Rough Idle
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects rough idle behaviour during the cold-start phase only. Once the engine has warmed up the issue disappears. Typically caused by injector deposits, low compression on one cylinder when cold, or sticky valve guides.

causes.labelEn: Injector tip coked - poor cold spray pattern

records.titleEn: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
records.descriptionEn: During the cold-start strategy the ECU monitors exhaust temperature to ensure catalyst light-off. The measured EGT remains below the target threshold within the allowed time - heat-up strategy is not effective. Causes include excessive heat loss, very rich mixture cooling the exhaust, or a faulty EGT sensor.

causes.labelEn: Excessive heat loss between port and catalyst

records.titleEn: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The ECU monitors the vacuum supplied to the brake booster (either via a dedicated sensor or via intake manifold pressure). The level has dropped below the calibrated threshold; brake-pedal feel will be hard, and an electric vacuum pump may be commanded to restore vacuum.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum leak in booster line or check valve

records.titleEn: Closed Throttle Position Switch
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated closed-throttle switch (or closed-throttle bit on the TPS) does not behave as expected - either it never activates, never deactivates, or shows incoherent state against TPS voltage and engine load. Used by older systems for fuel-cutoff and idle recognition.

causes.labelEn: Switch out of adjustment or worn

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the idle air control valve - open or short on supply, signal or ground. The ECU loses control of idle bypass airflow.
symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Starter Request Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The starter request input - the signal that tells the ECU the driver wants to crank the engine - shows a circuit fault. Without it the engine cannot be started under software-managed start strategies (stop-start, push-button, immobiliser-coordinated start).

records.titleEn: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
records.descriptionEn: The immobiliser system has detected a key that is not authorised for this vehicle. Engine start is blocked. Possible causes are an unprogrammed replacement key, a transponder fault, or a deliberate attempt to start with the wrong key.

records.titleEn: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: The battery temperature sensor reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with engine bay or coolant temperature. Modern alternator regulation uses battery temperature to adjust charging voltage, so an offset here causes over- or undercharging.
symptomsEn: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

records.titleEn: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the battery temperature sensor - open or short on supply, signal or ground.
symptomsEn: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

records.titleEn: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

records.titleEn: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0511 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Idle Air Control System Performance
records.descriptionEn: The idle air control system is electrically intact, but the actual idle airflow does not match the commanded value - typical for a sticky valve, intake leak, or carbon build-up around the throttle bore.

causes.labelEn: IAC valve sticking due to carbon

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the crankcase pressure sensor A - typically used to monitor PCV operation and detect a clogged separator or disconnected hose.

records.titleEn: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P051A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

records.titleEn: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P051A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P051A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P051A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: PCV Filter Restriction
records.descriptionEn: The pressure or flow sensor in the PCV path detects increased restriction across the oil-mist filter element. Once saturated with oil mist, the filter no longer passes blow-by gas, raising crankcase pressure and pushing oil past seals.

causes.labelEn: PCV filter saturated with oil mist

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine oil pressure sensor or switch reports values that are not plausible for current RPM, oil temperature, and engine load. Could indicate a sensor fault or genuinely abnormal pressure.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Low Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The oil pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum. Often points to an electrical fault — short to ground or failed sensor — but can also indicate genuinely low oil pressure.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0520 with the signal voltage above the plausible range - usually a short to supply or sensor failure that pegs the output high.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The ECU has determined that engine oil pressure is below the safe operating threshold. Caused by low oil level, worn oil pump, severe engine wear, or a stuck pressure relief valve. Continued operation can rapidly destroy the engine.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit to the cruise control servo (vacuum or electric actuator that holds throttle position) shows feedback in plausible range yet inconsistent with the commanded action - servo slow, sticking, or supply weak.

causes.labelEn: Servo response slow due to wear

records.titleEn: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault on the cooling fan tachometer feedback - the ECU loses fan speed information needed to verify cooling capacity and detect a stalled or runaway fan.

records.titleEn: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0526 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the commanded fan speed - typically sensor drift, weak magnet, or partial reluctor damage.

records.titleEn: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0526 with no detectable signal at all - sensor not producing pulses despite the fan being commanded on.

records.titleEn: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0526 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P052A with the phaser stuck retarded - cold-start strategy cannot pull the cam to the advanced position needed for fast catalyst light-off.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Same as P052B on bank 2. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: PCV Regulator Valve Performance
records.descriptionEn: The crankcase ventilation regulator valve - which throttles blow-by gas flow toward the intake based on engine load - is electrically intact but does not deliver the modelled pressure regulation. Either the valve diaphragm is fatigued or the spring is weak.

records.titleEn: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage
records.descriptionEn: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. The ECU uses this signal to enable the compressor and cooling fan; without it the A/C is typically disabled.

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The A/C refrigerant pressure sensor signal is implausible against operating conditions. Reading does not change as expected when the compressor cycles or ambient conditions change.

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage below the lower threshold — open, short to ground, sensor fault, or a refrigerant charge so low that the pressure is genuinely low.

causes.labelEn: Sensor circuit shorted to ground or open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage above the upper threshold — short to supply, defective sensor, or a system overcharge/blocked condenser causing genuine high pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Charge Loss
records.descriptionEn: The system detects an abnormally low refrigerant charge. Compressor operation is typically inhibited to prevent damage.

records.titleEn: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The evaporator temperature sensor signal is missing or out of range. Used to prevent icing of the evaporator core.

records.titleEn: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: The evaporator temperature sensor used to prevent evaporator icing reports a value within plausible range yet not matching the engine model or cabin conditions.

records.titleEn: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates a short to ground or sensor fault.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Typically open circuit or short to power.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0536 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The heater on PCV path A - used to prevent ice plugs in the crankcase ventilation hose during cold weather - has an open control circuit. Without it, condensation can freeze and block PCV flow, raising crankcase pressure dangerously.

causes.labelEn: Open in harness or heater element
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: PCV Heater A Performance
records.descriptionEn: The PCV heater on path A is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - hose temperature does not rise as commanded. Heater element aged or contact resistance increased.

records.titleEn: Crankcase Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: The crankcase pressure sensor reports a value above the safe upper threshold. Excessive crankcase pressure pushes oil past seals and contaminates the PCV path with mist - causes are clogged PCV system, frozen breather hose, or excessive blow-by from worn rings.

records.titleEn: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation. The pressure target on bank 1 is not reached within the calibrated time window - typical for a high-pressure pump that loses output when cold or a pressure regulator with cold-stickiness.

causes.labelEn: HP pump output low when cold

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

records.titleEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The intake air heater (grid heater) on path A - used on cold-start of diesel engines to warm intake air for reliable combustion - has an open control circuit. Without it, cold-start emissions and idle quality on cold days suffer.

causes.labelEn: Open in harness, relay or heater element
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 Low
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust gas temperature sensor signal at bank 1, sensor 1 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates short to ground or sensor fault.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 High
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust gas temperature sensor signal at bank 1, sensor 1 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Typically open circuit or short to power.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1: the signal voltage is below the expected range. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1: the signal voltage is above the expected range. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P052B on the B camshaft of bank 1. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Same as P052B on the B camshaft of bank 2. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
records.descriptionEn: At idle the ECU expects a calibrated fuel quantity to maintain set-speed. The actual quantity is significantly less than modelled - typical for a tight engine, very low friction, dragging accessory load missing, or implausible idle airflow.

records.titleEn: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
records.descriptionEn: Same as P054E with actual fuel quantity above the model - high friction, sticky throttle, or accessory drag.

records.titleEn: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the power steering pressure sensor. The ECU uses this signal to compensate idle speed when the steering load increases; without it idle stability can suffer during parking maneuvers.

records.titleEn: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The PS pressure sensor signal stays in electrical range but is implausible for the operating state, e.g. high pressure reported with the wheels straight.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input
records.descriptionEn: PS pressure sensor signal voltage below threshold — open, short to ground, or sensor failure. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor circuit shorted to ground or open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit High Input
records.descriptionEn: PS pressure sensor signal voltage above threshold — short to supply or sensor failure. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The power steering pressure sensor signal is intermittent. The ECM cannot consistently raise idle to compensate for steering load.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the brake booster pressure sensor - the ECU cannot determine vacuum reserve in the booster, which limits the safe operation of stop-start, regenerative-braking blending, and electric vacuum pump control.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0555 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - drift, partial blockage of the reference port.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0555 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0555 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0555 with intermittent or erratic signal. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P055A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P055A with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P055A with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

records.titleEn: Oxygen Sensor Control Module System Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated O2 sensor control module - found on systems with a wide-band sensor needing its own pumping current driver - reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Out of Range
records.descriptionEn: The measured oil pressure is far outside the expected range for current engine speed and oil temperature - either too low (oil pump weak, oil level low, bearing wear) or anomalously high (relief valve stuck closed, blocked oil cooler).

causes.labelEn: Oil pump worn or oil level low

records.titleEn: System Voltage Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A general fault in the system voltage seen by the ECU — value implausible, missing, or unstable but without crossing the specific thresholds of P0562 (low) or P0563 (high). Often appears intermittently with a marginal alternator or weak battery.

causes.labelEn: Charging system marginal (aged battery or alternator)
Corroded battery terminals or ground strap

records.titleEn: System Voltage Unstable
records.descriptionEn: The ECU monitors battery voltage and detects unstable behaviour - rapid fluctuations beyond what current load changes explain. Typical causes are a failing alternator, loose battery terminals, weak battery, or a heavy load (radiator fan, glow plugs, heated screen) drawing voltage down briefly.

records.titleEn: System Voltage Low
records.descriptionEn: Battery / charging system voltage seen by the ECU has dropped below the lower threshold (typically around 10.5 V). Modern ECUs are sensitive to under-voltage and may set this code briefly during cranking on a weak battery.

causes.labelEn: Corroded battery terminals or ground strap

records.titleEn: System Voltage High
records.descriptionEn: Battery / charging system voltage seen by the ECU exceeds the upper threshold (typically around 16 V). Caused by a failing voltage regulator inside the alternator. Sustained over-voltage can damage other electronics.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.labelEn: Open in stalk switch or harness

records.titleEn: Cruise Control On Signal
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an implausible state of the cruise control on/off signal - either the master switch is stuck on, intermittent, or shows a logic level that does not match other dash signals.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Cancel Input Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Cancel Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Resume Input Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Resume Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Set Input Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Set Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Coast Signal
records.descriptionEn: The coast (decelerate) signal of the cruise control reports an implausible state - typically a stuck or shorted contact.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects cruise-control operation.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects cruise-control operation.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Cancel Signal
records.descriptionEn: The cancel signal (driver-initiated cruise off) reports an implausible state - stuck, missing, or shorted.

causes.labelEn: Stalk or brake switch contact stuck

records.titleEn: Reductant Control Module System Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The reductant (AdBlue) control module reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window. Reductant dosing is suspended until voltage returns to range, which can drive NOx emissions out of compliance.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance
records.descriptionEn: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control B Performance
records.descriptionEn: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Accel Signal Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The cruise control accelerate input signal is implausible — switch contacts welded, wiring fault, or stalk defect. The ECU disables cruise control to prevent unintended acceleration.

records.titleEn: Brake Switch "A" Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: The brake light switch signal seen by the ECU is implausible — for example, both contacts active simultaneously, or no signal change despite the brake pedal being pressed (cruise control engages and disengages on this signal). On many cars also disables shift interlock.

causes.labelEn: Brake switch failed (worn contacts, internal break)
Switch misadjusted (does not actuate at correct pedal position)

records.titleEn: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control System Vehicle Speed Too High
records.descriptionEn: The cruise control sees actual vehicle speed exceed the set-speed by more than the diagnostic margin (typically going downhill or with throttle override). Persistent oversize means the system cannot bring speed down - either an actuator fault, brake-blending failure, or driver kick-down stuck.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Input Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on a cruise control input that is not specifically multiplexed - typically the dedicated set/resume button input.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Input Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0575 with the input voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Input Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0575 with the input voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0564 with the analogue level inside the plausible range yet not matching any of the calibrated button levels - resistor ladder drifted, contact resistance increased, or wrong stalk module fitted.

records.titleEn: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The brake pedal position sensor A has an open control circuit. The ECU loses analogue feedback about pedal travel - used by stop-start, regenerative braking and adaptive cruise to coordinate engine, motor and friction brakes.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P057A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the brake-light switch state - typical for a sensor offset against pedal travel or a worn potentiometer track.

records.titleEn: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P057A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P057A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P057A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Battery A State of Charge Performance
records.descriptionEn: The battery monitor reports a State of Charge (SoC) value that does not match the rest-voltage and current pattern - typically a battery near end of life, sulfation, or a deep discharge that the SoC algorithm has not converged on.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0564 with the analogue input voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0564 with the analogue input voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The vacuum-control solenoid of a vacuum-driven cruise servo (older systems) has an open control circuit - the servo cannot pull the throttle.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0582 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0582 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A and B Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Cruise control uses two redundant multiplexed inputs (A and B) for safety. The two inputs do not agree - one reports a button press the other does not, or both report incompatible levels at the same time.

causes.labelEn: Stalk module ageing - drift between A and B

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The vent solenoid of a vacuum-driven cruise servo - which releases vacuum to drop throttle - has an open control circuit. The servo cannot release vacuum, so cruise speed cannot be reduced.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0586 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0586 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects cruise-control operation.

causes.labelEn: Open in stalk switch or harness

records.titleEn: Battery Monitor Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: Battery Monitor Module Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. The module reports battery current, voltage and temperature for charge management.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

records.titleEn: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance
records.descriptionEn: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. The module reports battery current, voltage and temperature for charge management.

records.titleEn: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: The battery monitor module measures battery temperature above the safe upper threshold - charging is derated or stopped to prevent thermal runaway. Causes are heat soak from a hot engine bay, hard charging on a depleted battery, or a faulty sensor.

records.titleEn: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P058E with the temperature below the safe lower threshold - charging current is reduced to prevent damage to a frozen battery.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0579 on input B.

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0580 on input B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit High

records.titleEn: Restraints Deployed
records.descriptionEn: The restraint control module reports that one or more airbag or pretensioner stages have been deployed. The engine ECU latches this and runs the crash strategy - fuel cutoff, hazard lights, unlock central locking, disable cruise. The code can only be cleared after the restraint module is reset (typically requires module replacement).

records.titleEn: Vehicle Hardware Incompatibility
