records.titleEn: Cold Start Injection Timing Performance
records.descriptionEn: During cold-start the ECU adjusts injection timing (post-injection on diesels, intake-stroke timing on direct-injection petrols) to support catalyst light-off. The strategy does not deliver the expected timing - injector response slow or sensor offset.

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The reductant (AdBlue) heater control module - which warms tank, lines and injector to keep AdBlue from freezing - reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The supply line that powers the AdBlue dosing pump is open. Without supply the pump cannot deliver reductant pressure - dosing is suspended and NOx emissions can drift out of compliance.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05EE with the supply voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05EE with the supply voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The supply relay or driver for the reductant pump is welded or stuck active - the pump runs continuously, even with the engine off, draining the battery and over-pressurising the dosing circuit.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05EE with the supply stuck off - relay does not energise on command.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The power relay that supplies the entire exhaust aftertreatment system (DOC, DPF, SCR sensors and heaters) reports an open control circuit. Aftertreatment effectively goes offline.

causes.labelEn: Open in relay control or harness
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05F3 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05F3 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment power relay is stuck on - aftertreatment electronics stay powered after key-off, draining the battery.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05F3 with the relay not engaging on command.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: The reductant heater module is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - heater elements aged, supply line resistance, or thermostat sensor offset.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault on the stop-start status signal - the bus or hardwire that tells other modules whether the engine is auto-stopped or running.

records.titleEn: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05F9 with the signal shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P05F9 with the signal shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation. The pressure target on bank 2 is not reached within the calibrated time window - typical for a high-pressure pump that loses output when cold or a pressure regulator with cold-stickiness.

causes.labelEn: HP pump output low when cold

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control A Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: The boost control actuator A reports excessive operating temperature - typically heat soak from the turbo housing, prolonged high-load operation, or insufficient cooling. Boost is derated to protect the actuator electronics.
symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position. Active grille shutters manage airflow for engine cooling and aerodynamics.

causes.labelEn: Shutter jammed by debris or ice
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Brake Pressure Sensor and Brake Pedal Position Sensor Correlation
records.descriptionEn: The brake pressure sensor and pedal position sensor disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance - one indicates pedal action without the other showing pressure, or vice versa.

records.titleEn: Serial Communication Link
records.descriptionEn: A general fault on a serial communication link - typically used by older single-wire diagnostic protocols (KWP2000, ISO 9141) before CAN became universal. ECU has lost or corrupted communication with another module.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
records.descriptionEn: The ECU's internal memory checksum does not match the expected value at startup — the firmware/calibration in flash has become corrupt. Often appears after a failed flash, low battery during programming, or genuine module hardware failure.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Control Module Programming Error
records.descriptionEn: The ECU is reporting that it is missing required calibration data — typically appears after a virgin module is installed but never coded/programmed for the vehicle, or after a flash that did not write all blocks.

causes.labelEn: Replacement ECU not coded to vehicle

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detected a fault in its KAM (battery-backed memory used to store adaptations and DTCs). Often appears after battery disconnect or low battery; persistent codes indicate an internal ECU fault.

causes.labelEn: Battery disconnected or voltage too low
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
records.descriptionEn: ECU self-test detected a RAM fault during runtime checks. This is an internal ECU defect; replacement or reflash with manufacturer support is generally required.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
records.descriptionEn: ECU self-test detected a ROM/checksum failure on the program memory. The control software cannot be trusted; vehicle typically defaults to limp-home with reduced function.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
records.descriptionEn: The ECU's internal processor self-test has failed. This is a hard module fault — the ECU usually triggers limp-home mode and may not respond to scan tools fully until replaced or repaired.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECM performs an internal self-test and detects a processor or memory performance fault that does not fit the more specific P0601 to P0606 codes.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Control Module VSS Output A
records.descriptionEn: The vehicle speed signal output from the control module to other systems is faulty. Other modules expect a speed signal that the ECM no longer provides correctly.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Control Module VSS Output B
records.descriptionEn: A fault is detected on the secondary vehicle speed signal output (VSS B) that the ECU sends to other modules (instrument cluster, ABS, transmission). Output level inconsistent with the internal speed value.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
records.descriptionEn: Modern ECUs have a separate watchdog or monitoring processor that supervises the main processor. This processor reports a self-diagnosis fault - typically a watchdog event, ROM/RAM mismatch, or check-sum error in its monitor section. The ECU runs in a safety-fallback mode until repair.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module A and D Processing Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECU's analog-to-digital converter does not deliver consistent results - typically reference voltage drift, multiplexer fault, or noise on the analog ground.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Main Processor Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECU main processor self-diagnosis flagged a performance fault - watchdog, ROM check, or instruction-set self-test failed. Engine runs on safety strategy.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "accelerator pedal position" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Throttle Position Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle position" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Coolant Temperature Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine coolant temperature" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Control Module Vehicle Options Error
records.descriptionEn: The ECU's stored vehicle option configuration is invalid or does not match the connected hardware. Common after replacing or swapping a control module without proper coding/configuration.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: Modern direct-injection systems use a dedicated injector driver module that generates the high-voltage charge pulses needed to open piezo or solenoid injectors. The module reports an internal performance fault.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Control Module Relay Control
records.descriptionEn: A circuit fault on the relay that powers the injector driver module - either control line or contact integrity issue.
symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: TCM Processor
records.descriptionEn: The transmission control module performs an internal self-test and detects a processor performance fault.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: ECM and TCM Incompatible
records.descriptionEn: The ECM and TCM exchange identification or calibration data over the powertrain bus and detect that they are not a valid pair - typically appears after replacing one of the modules with a unit from a different vehicle variant.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Starter Relay Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the starter relay control circuit driven by the ECU/PCM. Typical symptom is a no-crank or intermittent crank condition.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Starter Relay A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The control line for starter relay A is shorted to ground - the ECU drives the relay and measures voltage too low.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Starter Relay Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The starter relay control circuit voltage is above the upper threshold — short to supply or stuck driver.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Control Module KAM Error
records.descriptionEn: The control module for alternative fuel (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) reports a Keep-Alive-Memory error - persistent calibration values are corrupt or unreadable. Adaptive learning is reset.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Control Module RAM and ROM Error
records.descriptionEn: The alternative fuel control module reports an internal RAM or ROM check failure - module no longer trustworthy.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Torque Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine torque" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Torque Calculation Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "torque calculation" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Engine RPM Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine speed (RPM)" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Engine Air Mass Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "intake air mass" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Brake Signal Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "brake signal" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Throttle Actuator Controller Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle actuator control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Generator Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault detected in the alternator/generator control circuit. The ECU regulates field excitation on most modern alternators; a fault here causes charging issues and may set additional battery voltage codes.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Lamp L Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit for the generator warning lamp output (L terminal) reports a fault.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Field F Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit for the generator field terminal (F) reports a fault. The ECM cannot regulate field current as expected.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Lamp Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Generic generator warning lamp control circuit fault, often used where the lamp terminal designation is not L or where multiple lamps share a single output.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit for the fuel cap warning lamp reports a fault. The ECM cannot drive the indicator that warns of an open or loose fuel cap.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Field Terminal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the alternator F terminal (field excitation) is below threshold — open or short to ground in the excitation path.

causes.labelEn: Field circuit open or shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Performance
records.descriptionEn: The generator field circuit response does not match command. Field current ramps slowly, drifts or fails to reach commanded values during regulation.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detected an open circuit in the fuel pump A control output. With no pump operation the engine cannot run; this code is often paired with no-start and no fuel pressure.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: The control output to the primary fuel pump A is electrically intact yet response and fuel pressure response do not match - typically a worn pump, a clogged strainer, or a partially shorted PWM driver.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "fuel injector control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Vehicle Speed Performance
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "vehicle speed" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The injector driver stage on bank 1 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.
symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The injector driver stage on bank 2 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.
symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module EEPROM Error
records.descriptionEn: The ECU's EEPROM (persistent calibration storage) reports a check-sum or write error. Calibration values may be corrupted - the ECU runs on safe defaults until repair.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM
records.descriptionEn: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM
records.descriptionEn: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Odometer Not Programmed ECM or PCM
records.descriptionEn: The odometer value stored in the ECM/PCM is missing or implausible - typical after a module replacement without odometer programming, or after persistent storage corruption.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Immobiliser Key Not Programmed
records.descriptionEn: The immobiliser system rejects the current key because it is not programmed to this vehicle. Engine start is inhibited.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High
records.descriptionEn: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Power Steering Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the power steering control output - typically the line that the ECU uses to request raised idle when steering load is high, or to enable an electric pump.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Power Steering Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Power Steering Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 1 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 2 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault is detected on the alternator voltage sense line A - the line over which the regulator measures battery-side voltage to set charging output.

causes.labelEn: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P063A with the sense voltage in plausible range yet not matching the alternator output - high contact resistance or wrong calibration.

causes.labelEn: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P063A with the sense voltage below the plausible range.

causes.labelEn: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P063A with the sense voltage above the plausible range.

causes.labelEn: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present
records.descriptionEn: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault on the intake air heater control - the ECU cannot drive the grid heater at cold-start.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The 5 V reference voltage that the ECU supplies to multiple sensors (TPS, MAP, accelerator pedal, etc.) has dropped out or is open-circuit. Symptoms cascade — many sensor codes appear at once, all related to the same reference rail.

causes.labelEn: Reference wire shorted to ground (one defective sensor pulls the rail down)
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The 5 V reference voltage on the A circuit (used by multiple sensors) is below threshold — short to ground or excessive current draw by a single sensor pulling the rail down.

causes.labelEn: Sensor or harness shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: 5 V reference rail A above threshold — short to a higher voltage source. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor or harness shorted to higher voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The serial communication line to the driver display (instrument cluster, MIL/check-engine warning) shows a circuit fault. Driver may not see warning lights as expected.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault on the A/C clutch relay control - the line over which the ECU engages the magnetic clutch to drive the A/C compressor.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Fuel Pump Control Module A
records.descriptionEn: A general fault is detected on the dedicated fuel pump control module A. Used on PWM-controlled returnless fuel systems to vary pump speed against demand. The module reports an internal performance issue.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: PTO Control Module
records.descriptionEn: A general fault on the power take-off (PTO) control module - reports internal performance issue or communication trouble. Affects vehicles with auxiliary mechanical drives (cranes, snow ploughs, hydraulic pumps).
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Glow Plug Control Module 1
records.descriptionEn: A general fault is detected on the first glow plug control module - typically a self-diagnosis flag for an internal driver, supply, or watchdog issue.
symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 1" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 2" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

records.titleEn: Unauthorized Software or Calibration Detected
records.descriptionEn: The ECU's secure boot or signature check has detected calibration data that is not signed by the manufacturer - typically appears after chip-tuning or unauthorised flash programming. The ECU may run on safe defaults or refuse to start.
symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Malfunction Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Malfunction
records.descriptionEn: A fault in the wiring or control circuit between the ECU and the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL). The MIL may stay on permanently, fail to light at key-on, or flicker — the OBD-II self-check on the bulb itself failed.

causes.labelEn: Wiring fault between ECU and cluster

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The 5-volt sensor reference rail B is open — the module supplies no voltage on this circuit. Every sensor powered from reference B loses its supply and reads invalid, so the ECU substitutes default values and may limit engine operation. Causes: a broken reference wire, a disconnected connector, or an internal open in the module's voltage regulator for rail B.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to supply or above the design voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

records.titleEn: Fuel Level Output Circuit

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 1

records.titleEn: Glow Plug Module Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit between the engine controller and the glow plug control module reports a fault. The ECU can no longer reliably command the module that drives the glow plugs, so cold-start pre-heating may not run. On a diesel this causes hard starting, white smoke, and rough running until warm. Causes: open or shorted wiring between ECU and glow plug module, a failed module, or a power/ground fault at the module.
symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit
records.descriptionEn: An electrical fault is present in the glow plug circuit for cylinder 1. The glow plug control module cannot drive this plug correctly — open circuit, short, or out-of-range resistance — so cylinder 1 is not pre-heated. On a cold start this causes hard starting, white smoke, and a misfire-like rough run until the engine warms. Causes: a failed glow plug, a broken supply lead to that plug, corrosion at the plug connector, or a faulty module output for cylinder 1.
symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Open

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Low

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit High

records.titleEn: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit - Loss of Direction Signal
records.descriptionEn: The output shaft speed sensor uses a quadrature output (two channels phase-shifted by 90°) so the TCM can determine direction of rotation. The direction channel is missing — TCM cannot tell whether the vehicle is rolling forward or backward, blocking neutral-idle and rollback-protection strategies.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit - Direction Error
records.descriptionEn: The TCM reads a direction from the output shaft speed sensor that contradicts the commanded gear — for example reverse direction while drive is engaged, or forward direction while reverse is engaged. Either the sensor wiring is swapped, the sensor is wrong, or the gear actually engaged is not the one commanded.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High

Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Modern transmissions can have two or more ATF temperature sensors (sump, cooler return, valve body). After a long key-off soak they should all read approximately the same ambient. The TCM detects an implausible spread between sensors — one of them drifts or is wired wrong.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Reverse 2 Incorrect Ratio

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift solenoid control circuit — used on manual-transmission performance vehicles to force a skip from 1st straight to 4th under low-load cruise (CAFE fuel-economy feature). With the input invalid the lockout cannot be applied.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Clutch position sensor A is electrically intact, but its readings drift away from the model — for example the position does not move when the actuator is commanded, or the offset shifts after a thermal cycle. Often a misadjusted sensor mount.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference voltage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High

Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on

Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Excessive Clutch A Slippage

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)

records.titleEn: Reverse Input Circuit

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Reverse Output Circuit

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Transmission Range Display Circuit

Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The hybrid control module detects an out-of-range signal from the temperature sensor of the inverter/motor electronics coolant loop. This sensor protects power electronics from overheating.

records.titleEn: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The motor electronics coolant temperature sensor reading is implausible relative to other thermal models or coolant flow estimates.

records.titleEn: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor Low Input
records.descriptionEn: Voltage at motor electronics coolant temperature sensor below threshold. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

records.titleEn: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor High Input

records.titleEn: Motor Torque Sensor Circuit High

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Reserved Powertrain Fault
records.descriptionEn: Manufacturer-specific reserved code in the SAE generic range used as catch-all for hybrid system faults that do not map to a more specific defined code. Should be diagnosed using the freeze frame data and any additional manufacturer codes.

records.titleEn: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 1 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.

causes.labelEn: Sulphur poisoning from high-sulphur fuel — desulphation regeneration not running
Thermal aging of washcoat after high-temperature exposure

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 2 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.labelEn: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted from runaway regeneration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.labelEn: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.

causes.labelEn: IMRC actuator or vacuum motor failed

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC flap on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position and cannot open at higher rpm. Top-end power suffers because the runner is restricted, and the engine may breathe poorly above mid-range.

causes.labelEn: Actuator stuck or vacuum line collapsed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart to P2006. The IMRC flap on bank 2 cannot return to the open position and chokes intake flow at higher rpm.

causes.labelEn: Carbon deposits seize flap closed on bank 2
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Open (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC solenoid for bank 1. No control current flows when the runner is commanded to switch, leaving the flap in its default position.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC solenoid drive line for bank 1 reads below the lower threshold — short to ground or a failed driver stage. The runner cannot be switched on demand.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 1 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

causes.labelEn: Actuator weak or vacuum supply low
Linkage worn — play between actuator and flap

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 2 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 1 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.

causes.labelEn: Excessive soot load triggers runaway regeneration
DPF temperature sensor reading drifts high

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 2 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 1 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.

causes.labelEn: Persistent misfire dumps unburned fuel into the cat
Sustained rich mixture from leaking injector or fuel pressure regulator

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 2 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage at the IMRC solenoid on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply or an open ground side. The solenoid is energised constantly or the driver protection trips.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is open or has lost continuity — control module no longer detects a closing path through the actuator winding.

causes.labelEn: Open wiring or chafed conductor in IMRC harness

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads below the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to ground or a stuck-low driver inside the control module.

causes.labelEn: Short to ground in driver line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads above the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground side.

causes.labelEn: Short to B+ in driver line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The position feedback signal of the IMRC flap on bank 1 is missing or implausible. Without feedback, the ECU cannot verify that the commanded runner position has been reached.

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor on bank 1 reports a value, but it does not match the commanded flap state — for example, the flap is commanded closed yet the sensor still reads open. Common on engines where the connector pin clip wears out and the sensor reads erratic positions.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads below the lower limit. Usually a short to ground on the signal wire or a failed sensor.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to supply, an open ground reference, or a sensor that failed high.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Open (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC position sensor on bank 2. Without position feedback the ECU cannot confirm runner switching and falls back to a default mode.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the commanded runner state — typically a sensor drift or sticking flap.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Unit 1)
records.descriptionEn: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Unit 1): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.

causes.labelEn: DEF crystallisation clogs the dosing nozzle

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Supply Voltage Low (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage feeding the IMRC actuator on bank 1 is below the lower limit — typically a fuse, relay, or harness fault on the supply rail.

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Supply Voltage Low (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage feeding the IMRC actuator on bank 2 is below the lower limit — typically a fuse, relay, or harness fault on the supply rail.

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Internal Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Internal self-diagnostics of the IMRC actuator on bank 1 report an off-spec condition — driver stage, position-feedback or thermal limit no longer matches the calibrated profile.

causes.labelEn: Actuator internal driver or sensor fault

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Internal Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Internal self-diagnostics of the IMRC actuator on bank 2 report an off-spec condition — driver stage, position-feedback or thermal limit no longer matches the calibrated profile.

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump A Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: Reductant Pump A Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.

causes.labelEn: Pump driver line shorted to B+
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a voltage above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or an open ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a signal above the upper plausibility limit — typically an open signal line, broken sensor, or short to B+.

causes.labelEn: Open signal line at IMRC position sensor

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a loose pin, partially-broken conductor, or moisture in the connector.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general fault is reported on the EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor circuit — open, shorted, or out of plausible range. The sensor is part of the evaporative-emission system used to monitor canister loading.

causes.labelEn: Harness fault between sensor and PCM

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Performance
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor reading is plausible but does not match expected behaviour over time or temperature — slow response, incorrect offset, or stuck reading.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor signal sits below the lower plausibility limit — short to ground or short between signal and ground inside the sensor.

causes.labelEn: Short to ground on signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit High Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor signal sits above the upper plausibility limit — open signal line, broken sensor, or short to B+.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP fuel-vapor temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a connector or chafed wire.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Fuel Fired Heater Disabled
records.descriptionEn: The fuel-fired auxiliary heater (used to warm coolant or DEF on cold start) has been disabled by the control module — typically because of repeated start failures, low-voltage supply, or a self-protection condition.

causes.labelEn: Fuel supply starved — empty tank or pump weak

records.titleEn: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The DEF tank heater control circuit is open or has lost continuity — the PCM cannot drive the resistive heater that prevents the DEF (urea) tank from freezing in winter.

causes.labelEn: Open wire between PCM and heater
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The DEF tank heater control line reads below the expected voltage — short to ground or stuck-low driver.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The DEF tank heater control line reads above the expected voltage — short to B+ or open ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Leakage
records.descriptionEn: A leak has been detected in the DEF (urea) supply system — usually by a pressure-decay test after pump shutdown, or by visible crystallisation around fittings.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Unit 1)
records.descriptionEn: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Unit 1): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The control line that gates the DEF supply pump or the regeneration heating circuit does not respond as commanded — duty cycle, current draw, or response time off-spec.

causes.labelEn: Supply relay aged or pitted contacts
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Fuel Fired Heater Performance
records.descriptionEn: The fuel-fired auxiliary heater is operating but not delivering the expected heat output within the calibrated time — flame sensor reports weak combustion, exhaust temperature does not rise, or coolant heating rate is below threshold.

causes.labelEn: Combustion chamber sooted from short cycles

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust gas temperature (EGT) sensor at position 2 on bank 1 — typically downstream of the catalyst or before the DPF — reports an implausible signal. EGT sensors protect the turbocharger and DPF from over-temperature and time the regeneration cycle.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The EGT sensor at bank 1 position 2 reads below the lower limit. Common when the signal is shorted to ground or the sensor element is open.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The EGT sensor at bank 1 position 2 reads above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply, an open ground or a sensor that drifted high — risk of false DPF over-temperature limp.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on the exhaust gas temperature (EGT) sensor at bank 2 sensor 2 — open, short, or out of plausibility. EGT sensors monitor catalyst, DPF, and turbocharger inlet/outlet temperatures.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The EGT sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 reads below the lower plausibility limit — short to ground or shorted sensor element.

records.titleEn: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 2)

records.titleEn: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 2)

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust
