records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit/Open: the control circuit is open. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Performance
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.
symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit for the dedicated aftertreatment fuel supply pump or solenoid is open — HC dosing into the exhaust will fail.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Performance
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel supply is electrically OK but does not deliver the commanded pressure or flow during regeneration — weak pump or partial blockage.

causes.labelEn: Pump weak — flow or pressure below threshold

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck open mechanically — fuel pressure cannot be cut off, risk of over-fueling exhaust.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck closed — HC dosing into exhaust fails, regeneration cannot raise temperature.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on the aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor — used to verify the dedicated HC-dosing rail is primed.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility fails — pressure does not rise during prime, drift across a regeneration.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Reductant Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The pressure in the SCR reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line is below the calibrated minimum. Without sufficient pressure the dosing module cannot atomise reagent properly, leading to NOx exceedence.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line pressure stays below the demanded value during dosing. The dosing system needs a stable supply pressure to inject metered amounts; without it the system cannot meet NOx targets.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: The reductant line pressure exceeds the upper limit. A blocked return path, a stuck pump or a faulty pressure sensor are common causes; over-pressure can damage the dosing valve and the pump head.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.labelEn: Exhaust leak between the two sensor positions

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: EGT sensors 1 and 3 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance — one is reading off, or there is a real temperature gradient that exceeds the calibrated map (e.g. from a leaking exhaust joint between the two locations).

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The DEF system air-assist pressure is below the required threshold — pump weak, line leak, or pressure-control valve stuck open.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: The DEF system air-assist pressure exceeds the upper threshold — pressure-control valve stuck closed or air pump runaway.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: Pressure in the AdBlue/DEF supply line is below the target. Usually a failing reductant pump, a clogged filter, frozen lines, or a leak in the pressurised circuit.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: Manufacturer-specific variant of the reductant over-pressure condition. The pressure exceeds the upper threshold during a defined operating window; on some platforms used in addition to P20E2 to flag a different test path.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit to the reductant (DEF) dosing pump is open — no current flow detected. Without pump pressure no AdBlue reaches the SCR catalyst and NOx reduction stops.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Reservoir Heater "A" Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the reductant tank heater "A" control circuit. AdBlue freezes at -11 C, so the tank heater must work for cold-start dosing.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: The reductant tank heater "A" does not heat when commanded on. Either a failed element or a stuck-off driver in the dosing module.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The reductant tank heater "A" stays energised even when not commanded — usually a shorted driver stage. Continuous heating wastes current and can overheat the heater element.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The SCR catalyst on bank 1 is no longer reducing NOx to the level the ECU expects, even with proper reductant dosing and quality. Often the result of catalyst poisoning by sulphur or hydrocarbons, thermal aging, or a leak between the upstream and downstream NOx sensors.

causes.labelEn: Exhaust leak between upstream and downstream NOx sensors

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Valve Performance
records.descriptionEn: The SCR reductant injection valve does not deliver the commanded amount of reagent. Causes include clogging by urea crystals, electrical faults or incorrect spray pattern.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.labelEn: Catalyst poisoning from sulphur or oil ash

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Reductant Consumption Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is below the model expectation — typically a clogged dosing nozzle, weak pump, or leak between pump and injector that recirculates DEF back to the tank.

causes.labelEn: Dosing nozzle clogged with crystallised DEF

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Consumption Too High
records.descriptionEn: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is above the model expectation — typically a leaking injector seat, leaking line fitting, or a pressure-control valve that vents constantly to the tank.

causes.labelEn: Injector seat leaks DEF into exhaust

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
records.descriptionEn: The DEF injection valve at bank 1 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
records.descriptionEn: The DEF injection valve at bank 2 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 1 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

records.titleEn: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The control line driving DEF pump B is open. On large engines or dual-tank systems a second pump (B) supplements pump A; with B offline the system loses redundancy.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: DEF pump B receives a run command but does not start, or shuts off prematurely.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: DEF pump B control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: DEF pump B control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Metering Unit 1 Performance
records.descriptionEn: The first DEF metering unit (the integrated module that combines pump, filter, level sensor, and dosing valve) is electrically OK but does not deliver the expected pressure or flow during operation.

causes.labelEn: Metering unit aged or partially clogged

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated SCR/reductant control module reports an internal performance fault — failed self-tests, watchdog resets, or calibration mismatch. Frequently a forerunner of total module failure.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive-by-wire throttle motor circuit is open — no current flow detected. The ECU loses authority over the throttle plate and forces a limp-home with reduced power.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The throttle motor responds, but its actual position does not track the commanded position within tolerance. Often a dirty throttle bore where the plate sticks, or a worn motor.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is below the lower limit. Typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage in the ECU.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Idle
records.descriptionEn: The ECU has detected a fault severe enough that it forces the throttle actuator to the idle stop. The driver loses pedal authority — only idle is available until the underlying TAC fault clears.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Engine Shutdown
records.descriptionEn: The TAC monitor commanded an engine shutdown because throttle authority can no longer be guaranteed safely. The most aggressive TAC limp mode — used when both throttle position sensors disagree or the motor is uncontrollable.

causes.labelEn: TPS1 and TPS2 disagree beyond limit

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited Power
records.descriptionEn: The TAC monitor restricts maximum throttle opening as a safety response to a TAC fault. The vehicle can still be driven, but accelerator pedal travel is capped.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Module Internal Processor
records.descriptionEn: The internal processor or watchdog of the throttle actuator control module reports an internal fault. Communication between the TAC monitor core and the main ECU core has failed plausibility — typical for a defective ECU.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: Self-tests within the TAC module fail their performance criteria — for example RAM/ROM checks or analog reference voltages drift. Indicates an aging ECU rather than a wiring fault.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor A signal at the closed-throttle stop does not match the learned minimum value. The mechanical or electrical zero reference of the throttle has drifted out of the expected range, often after cleaning, replacement or wear.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit of throttle actuator motor B is open. Throttle B is the secondary throttle on engines with two throttle bodies — typically used for tumble flap or charge-motion control.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Throttle actuator B motor responds electrically but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically high-resistance brushes, partial winding fault, or a sticky throttle bore.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
records.descriptionEn: The redundant throttle or accelerator pedal position channels C and F disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire systems compare two or three independent channels to detect a faulty potentiometer track.

causes.labelEn: One potentiometer track worn — voltage drift

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
records.descriptionEn: Throttle B control has detected an unsafe condition and forced an RPM limit. Common protective response when motor current, throttle position feedback, or supply voltage on the B path is out of spec.

causes.labelEn: Protection mode triggered by paired throttle-B fault

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited RPM
records.descriptionEn: The TAC monitor caps engine speed at a fixed limp-home rpm because it can no longer trust the throttle response. Driver may notice a hard rev limit well below redline.

causes.labelEn: Underlying TAC fault triggers rpm cap
Throttle response time out of spec

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: The throttle plate cannot be commanded back to the closed/idle position. Idle speed runs high or the engine cannot decelerate properly — safety-critical fault that usually triggers immediate limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The throttle plate cannot be commanded open. The engine stays at idle or stalls under load. Often caused by a seized motor, broken gear, or heavy carbon coking inside the throttle bore.

causes.labelEn: Throttle motor seized or gear broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Limited RPM
records.descriptionEn: The throttle actuator control has detected a fault and limits engine speed to a defined emergency value. The vehicle stays drivable but with severely reduced power until the underlying fault is cleared.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Below Limit RPM
records.descriptionEn: The throttle actuator system has dropped engine speed below the normal limp limit because of a more serious fault. The engine may run only at idle or stall.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor A is outside the expected range during the ECU self-check. The signal at fully closed throttle does not match the stored reference, indicating a mechanical or sensor issue.

causes.labelEn: Throttle plate sticking due to carbon

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor B does not match the learned reference during ECU self-test. Sensor B is the redundant channel used to cross-check sensor A.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: The minimum stop signal from throttle/pedal position sensor C is out of specification during initialization. Used on systems with three redundant sensor channels for safety-critical drive-by-wire control.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The current draw of the throttle motor lies outside the expected range — either much higher (binding plate) or much lower (worn brushes, open winding) than calibrated.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Closed Position Performance
records.descriptionEn: When commanded to idle, the throttle plate does not reach the calibrated closed position. Often a coked throttle bore preventing the plate from seating fully.

causes.labelEn: Throttle bore coked at closed-position stop
Plate or stop misadjusted after service

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: Throttle B is mechanically stuck open — typically carbon buildup or a broken return spring on the secondary throttle plate.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Throttle B is mechanically stuck closed — carbon buildup or a seized bearing on the secondary throttle.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Throttle B motor current draw does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The throttle B body itself does not respond as commanded — position feedback is plausible but does not track the setpoint within the calibrated time window.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
records.descriptionEn: The processor monitoring throttle B inside the throttle/PCM has reported a self-test failure — RAM check, ROM check, or watchdog timeout.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: The throttle control module on the B path reports general performance issues — internal fault, communication mismatch, or calibration drift.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the "C" channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor. Drive-by-wire pedals carry two or three redundant tracks; "C" is the third channel.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The "C" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the other channels or the operating point.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trim values on bank 1 indicate a lean condition during off-idle operation. The ECU has to add significant fuel correction to maintain stoichiometric mixture above idle.

records.titleEn: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 fuel trim shows a strong rich correction during off-idle operation. The ECU is forced to subtract fuel to keep the mixture near stoichiometric.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trims on bank 2 show a lean deviation during off-idle operating conditions. Causes are similar to bank 1 but isolated to the second cylinder bank.

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The supply rail to injector group G is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders. Causes: a broken supply wire, an open relay or fuse, or a disconnected group-G supply connector.

causes.labelEn: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage feeding injector group G has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out. Causes: a blown fuse, a failed injector supply relay, a voltage drop in the supply harness, or a poor ground or connector on the group-G supply.

causes.labelEn: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage on injector group G is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-G supply can mis-time or damage the injectors. Causes: charging-system overvoltage, a stuck supply relay or regulator, or a wiring fault shorting the group-G supply to a higher voltage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Cooling System Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine cooling system does not reach or maintain the expected temperature within the diagnostic window — usually a stuck-open thermostat, but also a low coolant level or a stuck cooling fan that overcools the engine.

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault is reported on engine coolant temperature sensor 2 — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor 2 is typically at the radiator outlet or as redundancy on the second cylinder bank.
symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: ECT sensor 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, stuck reading, or value does not track ECT 1 across a warm-up.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: ECT sensor 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The second coolant temperature sensor (often radiator-outlet or cylinder-head bank) reports a voltage above the upper threshold — typically an open signal wire or a sensor with infinite resistance.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The second coolant temperature sensor reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum leak (intake gasket, brake booster, hoses)

records.titleEn: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned

symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit signal B — used by anti-theft, immobiliser, or transmission to forbid throttle/fuel until released.

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Throttle/fuel inhibit B signal reads in range but plausibility fails — does not assert/release as expected.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit High

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Reductant No Flow Detected
records.descriptionEn: The DEF dosing system commands flow but the pressure or flow sensor reports no actual delivery — typically a fully blocked dosing nozzle, a frozen line, or a dead pump.

causes.labelEn: Dosing line or nozzle fully blocked
Line frozen at very low ambient temperature

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.

causes.labelEn: Leaking injector at idle on bank 2

symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

causes.labelEn: MAF reads low at high airflow

records.titleEn: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

records.titleEn: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

causes.labelEn: Sensor heater slow to warm up

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

records.titleEn: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
records.descriptionEn: The two intake air temperature sensors disagree by more than the calibrated correlation threshold during stable conditions. The ECU cannot determine which value is correct.

records.titleEn: Bank 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
records.descriptionEn: The fuel-trim values across cylinders on bank 1 differ enough that the bank-average air-fuel ratio is biased — a single cylinder is significantly leaner or richer than the rest. Detected by short-term-fuel-trim variance or by the wide-band O2 sensor harmonic monitor.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum leak at one intake runner

records.titleEn: Bank 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 1 reports a lean condition outside idle. On dual-injection systems (port + direct) the secondary loop trims port injection independently from the main loop.

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a lean condition outside idle. On dual-injection systems (port + direct) the secondary loop trims port injection independently from the main loop.

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a rich condition outside idle.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Secondary fuel control loop B reports a lean condition at idle on bank 1. Idle is sensitive to vacuum leaks since manifold flow is low.

causes.labelEn: Vacuum leak — most visible at idle

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.

causes.labelEn: Injectors leak at low duty cycle

symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Secondary fuel control loop B reports a lean condition at idle on bank 2. Idle is sensitive to vacuum leaks since manifold flow is low.

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary fuel control loop B reports a rich condition at idle on bank 2. Idle rich often means injectors that leak at low duty cycle.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Secondary fuel control loop B on bank 1 reports a lean condition at higher load. Lean at high load typically points at fuel pressure shortfall, restricted injectors, or charge-air leak.

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a lean condition at higher load. Lean at high load typically points at fuel pressure shortfall, restricted injectors, or charge-air leak.

causes.labelEn: Fuel or charge-air problem on bank 2

records.titleEn: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary fuel control loop B reports a rich condition at higher load on bank 2. Rich at high load typically points to a stuck-closed return on the fuel pressure regulator or over-delivering injectors.
symptomsEn: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The NOx sensor on bank 1 — typically upstream of the SCR catalyst — does not communicate or sends an invalid signal. NOx sensors are smart sensors with their own controller on the CAN bus; faults often involve heater failure or bus dropout.

causes.labelEn: Sensor wiring or CAN harness open

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The bank 1 NOx sensor reports values outside the plausibility window against modeled NOx and the downstream sensor. Often slow response from contamination by oil ash or coolant.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The NOx sensor signal on bank 1 is below the lower limit. Either short to ground on the analog return, sensor failed at low end, or pump cell stuck.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The NOx sensor signal on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground, or a sensor that failed high. SCR control runs in default mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The bank 1 NOx sensor signal drops out intermittently. Typical cause is a marginal connector, harness chafing near hot exhaust components, or thermal-cycling solder joints inside the smart sensor.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The heater inside the bank 1 NOx sensor cannot be controlled — open, short, or failed driver. Without proper heater operation the sensor never reaches its operating temperature and reports invalid data.

causes.labelEn: Heater short to supply or ground

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the bank 2 NOx sensor circuit. NOx sensors are smart sensors with a CAN/LIN interface; this code typically indicates that the sensor module no longer responds.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The bank 2 NOx sensor returns values outside the expected range for the operating point — for example a non-zero reading at engine off or unchanged values during load changes.

causes.labelEn: Sensor contaminated with soot or condensate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the heater of the bank 2 NOx sensor. NOx sensors must reach roughly 800 C to measure correctly; without heater current the sensor never enters its operating range.

causes.labelEn: Heater wiring open or connector loose

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The heater feedback (sense) line on the bank 2 NOx sensor reports values outside the expected window — heating is happening but the temperature does not match the model.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The heater control loop for the NOx sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reports off-spec behaviour — heater current draw or response time outside the calibrated range. NOx sensors only operate above ~600 °C, so heater control is critical.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The heater control loop for the NOx sensor at bank 1 sensor 2 reports off-spec behaviour — heater current draw or response time outside the calibrated range. NOx sensors only operate above ~600 °C, so heater control is critical.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The bank 2 NOx sensor reports correctly some of the time but intermittently drops out. Often a marginal connector, a wiring chafe or a sensor that fails when warm.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The heater sense line on the bank 2 NOx sensor produces intermittent readings. Often a thermal fault inside the sensor or a connector under temperature cycling.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The feedback line that monitors the NOx sensor heater current draw on bank 1 sensor 1 jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)

Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.
