symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The feedback line that monitors the NOx sensor heater current draw on bank 2 sensor 1 jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general fault in the barometric pressure sensor circuit. The atmospheric pressure value used for altitude compensation and fuel/air calculation is not available or implausible.

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The barometric pressure sensor delivers an electrically valid signal that does not match the operating point — for example pressure jumps that do not match altitude changes, or values stuck near full scale.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The barometric (ambient) pressure sensor reports a voltage below the valid window. The ECU uses this signal to compensate fuel and boost calculations for altitude — a stuck-low value tricks the ECU into thinking the car is at high altitude.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The barometric pressure sensor reports a voltage above the valid window. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on barometric pressure sensor B — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor measures atmospheric pressure for altitude compensation; sensor B is a redundant or secondary unit.

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor B below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor B above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
records.descriptionEn: Barometric pressure sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Used for redundancy on hybrid and emission-critical systems.

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage from the barometric pressure sensor is below the calibrated minimum. The signal is too low for any plausible atmospheric pressure, suggesting a short to ground or sensor fault.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The barometric pressure sensor reports a voltage above the upper limit. The signal cannot represent any realistic atmospheric pressure, indicating an open circuit or short to supply voltage.

causes.labelEn: Open in signal or ground wire
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 1 sensor 2 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.

causes.labelEn: Short between signal and heater wires

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 1 sensor 3 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.

causes.labelEn: Short between signal and heater wires

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 2 sensor 1 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.

causes.labelEn: Short between signal and heater wires

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 2 sensor 2 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.

causes.labelEn: Short between signal and heater wires

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: The O2 sensor signal wire on bank 2 sensor 3 has shorted to the heater wire. This pulls the signal away from a measurement of exhaust composition and produces erratic fuel-trim behaviour.

causes.labelEn: Short between signal and heater wires

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The pumping current line of the wide-band lambda sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is unable to operate. Wide-band sensors regulate exhaust oxygen to a reference cell via this pumping current — without it, AFR cannot be measured.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Pumping current at the bank 1 sensor 1 wide-band lambda probe is below the lower limit — short to ground or sensor at end of life.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Pumping current at the bank 1 sensor 1 wide-band lambda probe is above the upper limit — short to supply or open return path.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater E Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Reductant Heater E Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater F Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Reductant Heater F Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault. The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) heater keeps the urea fluid from freezing; a fault can impair SCR dosing in cold conditions.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The pumping current of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 1 is in electrical range but plausibility check fails. Wide-band sensors use a pumping cell that adjusts oxygen concentration in a reference chamber; the current required is proportional to lambda.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The pumping current of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 2 is in electrical range but plausibility check fails. Wide-band sensors use a pumping cell that adjusts oxygen concentration in a reference chamber; the current required is proportional to lambda.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Resistance Out Of Range (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The reference resistance of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 1 is outside the calibrated range — used by the controller to set the operating point of the pumping cell. Drift here indicates sensor element ageing or contamination.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Resistance Out Of Range (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The reference resistance of the wide-band O2 sensor on bank 2 is outside the calibrated range — used by the controller to set the operating point of the pumping cell. Drift here indicates sensor element ageing or contamination.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart of P2237. The wide-band lambda sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 cannot operate its pumping current circuit.

causes.labelEn: Pumping current line open on bank 2

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The pumping-current line of the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 2, sensor 1 is below the lower threshold. Wide-band sensors use a small pumping current to keep their measuring cell at lambda 1; a low value usually means an open or shorted pump cell.

causes.labelEn: Pump cell open or sensor failed
Pumping current line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The pumping-current line of the bank 2, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor reads above the upper threshold. Common with a short to a positive supply or a damaged sensor amplifier in the ECU.

causes.labelEn: Pumping current line shorted to positive
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The reference voltage line that powers the wide-band sensor cell on bank 1 sensor 1 is missing or out of tolerance. Without correct reference, the AFR calculation is invalid.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The reference voltage that the ECU supplies to the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 1, sensor 1 drifts outside the expected range. The reference is the baseline against which the cell voltages are measured; a drift falsifies every lambda calculation.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The reference voltage feeding the bank 1, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor is below the lower threshold. Often a short to ground in the wiring or a failed reference output stage.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The reference voltage on the bank 1, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor reads above the upper threshold. Common with a short to a positive supply or a corroded connector with leakage current.

causes.labelEn: Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart of P2243. Reference voltage on the bank 2 sensor 1 wide-band probe is missing or out of tolerance.

causes.labelEn: Reference voltage line open on bank 2

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart to P2244. The reference voltage at the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 2, sensor 1 is outside its expected range and falsifies the lambda calculation.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart to P2245. The reference voltage on bank 2, sensor 1 is below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or failed ECU output.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The measured heater element resistance of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is outside the calibrated range. Used as a sensor-element health check.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The measured heater element resistance of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 is outside the calibrated range. Used as a sensor-element health check.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit for the shutoff valve at the alternative-fuel tank A is open. Bi-fuel vehicles (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) use a high-pressure shutoff valve at the tank for safety; with this fault the alternative fuel cannot be drawn from the tank.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: Alternative-fuel shutoff valve A is electrically OK but does not open when commanded. Vehicle remains on petrol/diesel only.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Shutoff valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Shutoff valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart to P2246. The reference voltage at bank 2, sensor 1 is above the upper threshold, usually due to a short to positive or connector leakage.

causes.labelEn: Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The negative current control line (Vs−) of the wide-band lambda sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is open or out of range. Used as the virtual ground reference for the Nernst cell.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The negative-current (Vs negative) line on the bank 1, sensor 1 wide-band oxygen sensor is below the lower threshold. This line is the return path for the Nernst cell; loss of the signal blocks the lambda calculation.

causes.labelEn: Vs negative line shorted to ground
Nernst cell return open inside sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The Vs negative line on bank 1, sensor 1 reads above the upper threshold. Often a short to positive or a damaged ECU sensor amplifier.

causes.labelEn: Vs negative line shorted to positive
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart to P2252. The Vs negative line on the wide-band oxygen sensor at bank 2, sensor 1 is below the lower threshold.

causes.labelEn: Vs negative line shorted to ground
Nernst cell return open inside sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 counterpart to P2253. The Vs negative line on bank 2, sensor 1 reads above the upper threshold.

causes.labelEn: Vs negative line shorted to positive
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a low-side voltage below threshold on the heater control of the rear oxygen sensor on bank 1. The heater driver may be stuck on or shorted to ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light on after several drive cycles
Slightly increased fuel consumption during cold start
Delayed entry into closed-loop fuel control

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Control A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit of the secondary air injection system A reads a voltage below specification. Either the relay output is shorted to ground or the wiring/load is faulty.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Control A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit A of the secondary air injection system shows a voltage above the calibrated upper threshold. Likely a short to battery voltage or an open in the relay coil/output.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The drive line for secondary air injection (AIR) control circuit B is stuck low. Secondary air is pumped into the exhaust manifold during cold start to speed up catalyst light-off.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The factory calibration memory of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 cannot be read or contains a checksum error. Each NOx sensor ships with a unique calibration table programmed at the factory.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The factory calibration memory of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 cannot be read or contains a checksum error. Each NOx sensor ships with a unique calibration table programmed at the factory.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 1): the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

causes.labelEn: Sensor poisoned by silicon, sulphur, or oil ash
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1): the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 reads suspiciously high for too long — biased upward or stuck. Common after sensor poisoning by silicon, sulphur, or oil ash.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 reads suspiciously low for too long — biased downward or stuck. Common after sensor element ageing, condensate damage from cold start, or wiring fault that pulls the signal down.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: AIR system control B drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Turbo/Super Charger Bypass Valve Mechanical
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a mechanical fault in the turbocharger or supercharger bypass valve. The valve does not open or close as commanded, causing boost-pressure errors and reduced engine response.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbo Boost Pressure Not Detected - Mechanical
records.descriptionEn: The ECU does not detect any meaningful boost pressure increase under load even though the turbocharger is commanded. Likely a mechanical defect in the turbo, charge-air piping or wastegate.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbo/Super Charger Boost System Performance
records.descriptionEn: Boost pressure does not match the requested target during normal operation. The deviation between commanded and measured boost exceeds the calibrated tolerance, often due to leaks, sticking actuators or sensor errors.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the diesel water-in-fuel sensor circuit. Until repaired, water contamination in the fuel filter cannot be detected, risking damage to the high-pressure pump and injectors.

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects that the water-in-fuel sensor signal is implausible compared to operating conditions. The reading does not change as expected during fuel filter purge or warm-up.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The water-in-fuel sensor at the diesel fuel filter reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The sensor warns the driver to drain the filter when condensate accumulates.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Water-in-fuel sensor reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Water-in-fuel sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Condition - Sensor A
records.descriptionEn: The water-in-fuel sensor at fuel filter A has detected water above the warning threshold. The fuel filter must be drained; running the engine on water-contaminated diesel can damage the high-pressure pump and injectors.

causes.labelEn: Condensate accumulated in filter — drain required

records.titleEn: Water in Fuel Lamp Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the drive line for the dashboard water-in-fuel warning lamp.

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Boost Pressure Too High - Mechanical
records.descriptionEn: Boost pressure on turbo A exceeds the upper threshold and the cause is mechanical (wastegate stuck closed, VGT vanes stuck closed) rather than electrical drive fault.
symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response
records.descriptionEn: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The DPF substrate on bank 1 has been detected as cracked, melted, or removed. Differential pressure across the filter is too low for the measured exhaust flow — the soot trap no longer works.

causes.labelEn: Substrate cracked or melted from runaway regen

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The DPF substrate on bank 2 has been detected as cracked, melted, or removed. Differential pressure across the filter is too low for the measured exhaust flow — the soot trap no longer works.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response
records.descriptionEn: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports a constant lean signal during a forced-rich command from the ECU. Suggests either a sensor that has lost its rich-side response, or a catalyst that is so degraded that no rich exhaust reaches the downstream sensor (cross-check P0420).

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports a constant rich signal during a forced-lean command. Suggests a failed downstream sensor or a sensor contaminated by oil/coolant from upstream engine wear.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 reports a constant lean signal during a forced-rich command from the ECU. Suggests either a sensor that has lost its rich-side response, or a catalyst that is so degraded that no rich exhaust reaches the downstream sensor (cross-check P0420).

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 reports a constant rich signal during a forced-lean command. Suggests a failed downstream sensor or a sensor contaminated by oil/coolant from upstream engine wear.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 3): the control module has detected this fault condition.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 3): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.labelEn: Sensor coated with carbon or fuel residue

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: O2 sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 reports a lean reading suspiciously stable for too long. Sensor 3 is typically downstream of the second catalyst on systems with three-stage aftertreatment.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
records.descriptionEn: O2 sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 reports a rich reading suspiciously stable for too long. Sensor 3 is typically downstream of the second catalyst on systems with three-stage aftertreatment; sensor coated with carbon or fuel residue is the typical cause.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 3 / Bank 2 Sensor 3
records.descriptionEn: The PCM detects that the O2 sensor signals from bank 1 sensor 3 and bank 2 sensor 3 are swapped — typically a wiring crossover after sensor replacement.

records.titleEn: Intake Air System Leak
records.descriptionEn: The ECU has detected a discrepancy between commanded throttle/intake conditions and the resulting MAP/MAF that points to unmetered air entering after the throttle body. On turbocharged engines this often means a cracked or disconnected boost pipe between turbo and intake; on naturally aspirated engines, a hole in the intake manifold or hose.

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on barometric pressure sensor C — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor measures atmospheric pressure for altitude compensation; sensor C is a redundant or secondary unit.

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor C reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor C below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor C above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Barometric sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Restriction or leak detected in the intake plumbing between the air filter and the mass-air-flow sensor on bank 2 — typically a cracked intake boot or torn filter element.

records.titleEn: Air Flow Restriction / Air Filter Restriction
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an excessive intake restriction. Either the air filter is heavily clogged or an obstruction in the intake duct is reducing airflow below the expected level.

records.titleEn: Air Leak Between MAF and Throttle Body
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects unmetered air entering between the mass airflow sensor and the throttle body. The actual airflow into the engine is greater than what the MAF measures, leading to lean conditions.

records.titleEn: Air Leak Between Throttle Body and Intake Valves
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects unmetered air entering downstream of the throttle body. Typical sources are leaking intake-manifold gaskets, vacuum hoses or PCV components.

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the injector control pressure (ICP) sensor — used on HEUI (Hydraulically actuated Electronically controlled Unit Injector) systems on heavy-duty diesel engines such as the Ford Powerstroke 6.0/7.3 and Caterpillar engines. ICP measures the high-pressure oil that actuates the injectors.

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The injector control pressure (ICP) sensor on HEUI diesel systems reports a value that does not match expected operating range or commanded pressure. Affects fuel injection timing and quantity.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The voltage of the injector control pressure sensor is below the calibrated minimum. The signal indicates either a short to ground or a sensor that has lost its supply.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The voltage of the injector control pressure sensor is above the calibrated maximum. Likely a short to supply voltage or an open ground in the sensor circuit.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The injector control pressure sensor signal is intermittently lost or out of range. Often caused by intermittent wiring faults or a failing sensor that drops out under vibration or temperature.

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: ICP is above the upper threshold during operation. Typically the injection pressure regulator (IPR) is stuck closed or the high-pressure oil pump runs above target.

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Too High - Engine Off
records.descriptionEn: ICP remains above threshold after engine shutdown — pressure does not bleed off as expected, indicating a stuck check valve or sensor offset error.

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High

causes.labelEn: Return path blocked or pump runaway

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
records.descriptionEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low: the adaptive learning value has reached its lower limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: ICP is below the lower threshold — typically IPR stuck open, leaking high-pressure oil rail, or weak HP oil pump.

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
records.descriptionEn: During cranking, ICP does not build up enough to fire injectors. Typical no-start condition on HEUI engines from a stuck-open IPR or weak HP oil pump.

causes.labelEn: HP oil rail does not pressurise

records.titleEn: Injector Control Pressure Erratic
records.descriptionEn: ICP signal is unstable or jumps — connector or sensor issue, or air in the high-pressure oil rail. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Performance
records.descriptionEn: The high-pressure fuel pressure regulator (volume control or pressure control valve on a direct-injection rail) is not maintaining commanded pressure. Often the rail-pressure sensor reading drifts away from the setpoint under load.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Electrical fault on the control line to the high-pressure fuel pressure regulator solenoid. Without a working drive signal the rail cannot maintain pressure and the engine may not start or runs in limp-home.
symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage to the second fuel pressure regulator solenoid is below the lower limit. On common-rail diesels and direct-injection petrol engines this affects high-pressure fuel control directly.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage to the second fuel pressure regulator solenoid is above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. The driver protection trips, regulator falls back to default.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: During engine deceleration with closed throttle (DFCO), the O2 sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 should swing fully lean as the manifold fills with fresh air. Code is set when the swing does not happen — usually a slow or coated sensor.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: During engine deceleration with closed throttle (DFCO), the O2 sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 should swing fully lean as the manifold fills with fresh air. Code is set when the swing does not happen — usually a slow or coated sensor.

records.titleEn: Brake Pedal Position / Accelerator Pedal Position Correlation
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects simultaneous brake and accelerator activation beyond a permitted threshold. Modern brake-throttle override safety logic forces idle in this state — usually triggered by a stuck brake light switch or a faulty pedal sensor.

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The drive circuit for the turbocharger compressor outlet valve (also called diverter valve or blow-off valve) is open. The valve releases boost pressure when the throttle closes to prevent compressor surge.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Compressor outlet valve drive line stuck low — short to ground. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Stuck Open

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Stuck Closed

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 responds too slowly when NOx concentration rises (typically observed when SCR dosing is reduced or stopped). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.

causes.labelEn: Sensor aged or protection cap clogged
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response High to Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 responds too slowly when NOx concentration falls (typically observed when SCR dosing increases). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Sensing Element (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The wide-band sensing element of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 reports an internal performance fault — typically poisoning, condensate damage, or end of service life.

causes.labelEn: Element poisoned or end of life
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
records.descriptionEn: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 responds too slowly when NOx concentration rises (typically observed when SCR dosing is reduced or stopped). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The downstream NOx sensor on bank 1 (post-SCR) responds too slowly when NOx levels fall after a reductant injection event. The control unit measures the time between commanded reductant dose and the resulting NOx drop and finds it exceeds the diagnostic threshold, indicating an aged sensor element.

causes.labelEn: NOx sensor element aged or thermally damaged
SCR efficiency reduced (catalyst aged or contaminated)

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element poisoned by silicone, sulphur or oil ash
Thermal shock from condensate (cold start with wet exhaust)
Sensor at end of service life

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The temperature sensor at the SCR catalyst inlet reports a value below the threshold needed for efficient ammonia conversion. Below roughly 180-200 °C the SCR cannot reduce NOx and reductant injection is suspended; if this is detected continuously the ECU sets the fault.

causes.labelEn: Temperature sensor drifts low or has shifted resistance
Short-trip operation - exhaust never reaches operating temperature
Exhaust heater or heat-management strategy not active

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The primary control circuit of ignition coil A reads a voltage below the expected level — usually a short to ground on the primary driver wire or a low-resistance fault in the coil primary winding. Coil A cannot build a normal charge, so the cylinder it fires misfires, especially under load. Causes: short to ground in the primary wiring, an internal coil primary fault, or a faulty ECU/igniter driver.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The primary control circuit of ignition coil A reads a voltage above the expected level — typically an open primary circuit or a short to battery voltage on the primary control wire. The ECU sees no normal current flow, coil A does not fire, and the cylinder misfires. Causes: an open or disconnected primary wire, an internal open in the coil, or a faulty ECU driver.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil A Secondary Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A fault is detected on the secondary (high-voltage) side of ignition coil A. The spark delivered to the plug is missing or too weak, causing a misfire on the cylinder served by coil A. Causes: a worn spark plug or wide gap, a cracked coil or boot, carbon tracking, or an open or leaking secondary winding.

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The ECU reads a low primary control voltage on ignition coil B. Misfire is typically observed on the cylinder this coil serves.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil B Primary Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the primary control of ignition coil B exceeds the calibrated upper limit, indicating an electrical fault that prevents proper coil charging.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil B Secondary Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The secondary side of ignition coil B is faulty. Spark energy at the corresponding spark plug is insufficient, producing misfires.

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The primary control of ignition coil C reads below the calibrated minimum. The cylinder served by this coil will misfire.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil C Primary Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The primary control voltage at ignition coil C exceeds the upper limit, suggesting a short to battery or an open primary winding.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil C Secondary Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The secondary side of ignition coil C does not produce sufficient spark energy. Misfire is observed on the corresponding cylinder.

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil D Primary Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Low primary control voltage on ignition coil D. The cylinder served by this coil will misfire if not corrected quickly.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance Adjustment At Limit During Balance
records.descriptionEn: The ECU continuously trims individual cylinders to equalise air-fuel ratio across the bank using ion-current or per-cylinder lambda feedback. For cylinder 1 the per-cylinder fuel correction has hit its software-side maximum or minimum without restoring balance, indicating the underlying mechanical or fuelling deviation is too large to compensate.

causes.labelEn: Fuel injector for cylinder 1 has drifted in flow rate
Local intake or vacuum leak at cylinder 1
Partial misfire from ignition or fuel-side defect

For cylinder 10 the per-cylinder fuel correction has hit its software-side maximum or minimum without restoring balance, indicating the underlying mechanical or fuelling deviation is too large to compensate.

causes.labelEn: Fuel injector for cylinder 10 has drifted in flow rate

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil G Secondary Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A fault is detected on the secondary (high-voltage) side of ignition coil G. The spark delivered to the plug is missing or too weak, causing a misfire on the cylinder served by coil G. Causes: a worn spark plug or wide gap, a cracked coil or boot, carbon tracking, or an open or leaking secondary winding.

causes.labelEn: Spark plug worn, fouled or with excessive electrode gap

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil H Primary Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The primary control circuit of ignition coil H reads a voltage below the expected level — usually a short to ground on the primary driver wire or a low-resistance fault in the coil primary winding. Coil H cannot build a normal charge, so the cylinder it fires misfires, especially under load. Causes: short to ground in the primary wiring, an internal coil primary fault, or a faulty ECU/igniter driver.

causes.labelEn: Primary winding shorted to ground or harness chafed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Coil H Primary Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The primary control circuit of ignition coil H reads a voltage above the expected level — typically an open primary circuit or a short to battery voltage on the primary control wire. The ECU sees no normal current flow, coil H does not fire, and the cylinder misfires. Causes: an open or disconnected primary wire, an internal open in the coil, or a faulty ECU driver.

causes.labelEn: Open circuit in primary winding or harness for coil H
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cylinder 1 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 1 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 2 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 2 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 3 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 3 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 4 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock sensor channel for cylinder 4 has registered combustion noise above the calibrated knock threshold beyond what the spark retard map can correct. Often associated with low-octane fuel, EGR malfunction or carbon-induced hot spots.

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an open circuit on the control line for the third (C) fuel pressure regulator. Either the regulator solenoid coil is internally open, the harness is broken, or the connector has lost contact - the ECU cannot drive the regulator and rail pressure cannot be controlled by this stage.

causes.labelEn: Open circuit in harness or connector
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P233A but with the control line shorted to ground - the ECU measures a low voltage that does not match the commanded duty cycle.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P233A but with the control line shorted to supply - the ECU measures a high voltage that does not match the commanded duty cycle.

causes.labelEn: Control line shorted to battery or supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is open. Without supply the regulator cannot operate and the ECU cannot maintain rail pressure on this stage; sets when the controller sees no current flow even with the solenoid commanded on.

causes.labelEn: Supply line open or relay defective
Fuse for regulator B supply blown
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is below the expected voltage with the regulator commanded active - typically a high-resistance feed, partial short to ground or weak relay contact.

causes.labelEn: Supply feed has high contact resistance
Partial short to ground on supply line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P233D but with the supply line shorted to a higher potential than expected, so the ECU measures more voltage on the regulator B feed than the commanded level allows.

causes.labelEn: Supply line shorted to a higher voltage rail
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

records.titleEn: Cylinder 5 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock-sensor evaluation reports cylinder 5 above the knock threshold over a sustained window. The ECU retards ignition for that cylinder; persistent knock indicates poor fuel quality, carbon deposits or cooling issues.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 6 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: Same condition as P2340 but on cylinder 6 — sustained knock above the threshold with retarded ignition correction.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 7 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: Sustained knock above the threshold on cylinder 7 — usual causes are fuel quality, carbon deposits, or cooling issues at this cylinder.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 8 Above Knock Threshold
records.descriptionEn: Sustained knock above the threshold on cylinder 8 — typical on V8 engines under load with poor fuel.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock or combustion-vibration sensor monitors the structure-borne noise of each cylinder. The signal level for cylinder 9 has stayed above the diagnostic threshold for an extended period, indicating either persistent knock or an electrical fault that biases the channel high.

causes.labelEn: Persistent knocking on cylinder 9 (low-octane fuel, carbon deposits, hot spot)
Sensor or wiring biased high by short or moisture
Mechanical knock from bearings, piston pin or wrong torque

records.titleEn: Cylinder 10 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The knock or combustion-vibration sensor monitors the structure-borne noise of each cylinder. The signal level for cylinder 10 has stayed above the diagnostic threshold for an extended period, indicating either persistent knock or an electrical fault that biases the channel high.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

records.titleEn: Cylinder 11 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

records.titleEn: Cylinder 12 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the cylinder 9 combustion pressure sensor — used on engines with closed-loop combustion control (e.g. some Volvo and BMW direct-injection diesels) to measure cylinder pressure directly via a sensor at the glow plug or injector position.

causes.labelEn: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Sensor signal implausible against engine model
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 9 pressure sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or wiring issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Intermittent contact at connector or terminal
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 9 measured peak combustion pressure is below the calibrated minimum — typically low compression, weak injection, or stuck-open exhaust valve.

causes.labelEn: Low compression on cylinder 9 (valves, rings, head gasket)

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 9 measured peak combustion pressure is above the calibrated maximum — typically pre-ignition, knock, over-fuelling, or runaway combustion.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Variation Low
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder-to-cylinder pressure variation on cylinder 9 is below the calibrated minimum — pressure stays unusually constant cycle-to-cycle, often a sign that the closed-loop combustion controller has lost authority or the sensor signal is filtered.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Pressure Variation High
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder-to-cylinder pressure variation on cylinder 9 is above the calibrated maximum — combustion is unstable cycle-to-cycle, typical of partial misfire or injector seat erosion.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Combustion Performance
records.descriptionEn: The closed-loop combustion controller reports that combustion performance on cylinder 9 is below the calibrated quality metric. Computed from the cylinder pressure trace — IMEP (indicated mean effective pressure), CA50 (50% mass burnt angle) or peak pressure deviates from the model.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Heater Control Module Power Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P23C7 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Heater Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The fuel rail heater - on common-rail diesels for cold-start - has an open control circuit. The rail cannot be heated, slowing cold-start fuel atomisation.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: Fuel Rail Heater Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P23CA with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Fuel Heater Control Module Feedback Signal Open

records.titleEn: Fuel Heater Control Module Feedback Signal Performance

records.titleEn: Fuel Heater Control Module Feedback Signal Circuit Low

records.titleEn: EGR C Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: A general open-circuit fault on the third EGR valve C control - typically a third EGR loop in heavy-duty engines or specific Euro-7 systems.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: EGR C Control Circuit Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P23E1 with the actuator electrically intact but not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: EGR valve C sticking due to soot

records.titleEn: EGR C Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P23E1 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR C Control Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: EGR valve C is stuck in the open position - exhaust gas continuously dilutes intake air, reducing power and risking misfires at idle.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: EGR C Control Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: Same as P23E5 with valve C stuck closed - no EGR through this stage; NOx emissions rise. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: EGR C Flow Insufficient Detected

causes.labelEn: EGR cooler C clogged with soot

records.titleEn: EGR C Flow Excessive Detected
records.descriptionEn: Same as P049C on EGR loop C. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

symptomsEn: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

records.titleEn: Bank 1 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
records.descriptionEn: The secondary fuel system B on bank 1 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 1 is biased by an offset on the B system.

records.titleEn: Bank 2 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance

records.titleEn: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit to the EVAP leak-detection pump is open. Without that pump the ECU cannot pressurise the fuel-vapour system to test for leaks.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is below the lower limit. Often a short to ground in the harness.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or open ground.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The leak detection pump (LDP) - which actively pressurises the EVAP system to find leaks - has an open sense circuit. The ECU cannot read the pump status during the diagnostic cycle.

causes.labelEn: Open in pump or sense wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The sense (reed-switch or current-feedback) signal from the leak-detection pump is electrically valid but does not match expectations during a leak test. Often a worn pump diaphragm or a sticking reed contact.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The leak detection pump returns a sense signal that is electrically valid but does not match the expected response during the pump's self-test or pressure cycle.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: On vehicles with a sensed fuel cap, the cap-status signal is electrically valid but does not change as expected when the cap is opened or closed.

causes.labelEn: Cap seal aged, switch never seats
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: The sensor or switch that detects whether the fuel cap is properly closed reports a value within plausible range yet not matching driver action.

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The leak detection pump heater - keeps the pump diaphragm warm in cold weather - has an open control circuit.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
records.descriptionEn: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak
records.descriptionEn: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

causes.labelEn: Hose, fitting or cylinder valve leak

records.titleEn: EGR Slow Response
records.descriptionEn: The EGR system reacts to commanded changes more slowly than calibrated - typically a partly clogged EGR cooler, sticky valve, or worn actuator.

records.titleEn: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Stuck
records.descriptionEn: The fuel cap status switch is stuck in one position — the ECU never sees the expected transition between open and closed.

records.titleEn: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the fuel cap sensor/switch circuit — open or short.

records.titleEn: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
records.descriptionEn: Same as P2409 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Recirculation System Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECU monitors EGR flow indirectly through MAF, MAP or differential-pressure feedback and finds that actual EGR flow does not match the commanded value over a sustained period.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P237A but on the upstream sensor B1S1 (pre-catalyst). A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

records.titleEn: EVAP Switching Valve Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an open circuit on the EVAP switching valve drive line. The valve cannot be commanded between its purge and isolation positions.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Switching Valve Performance
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP switching valve responds electrically but does not produce the expected pressure change. Often a stuck valve seat or a torn diaphragm.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP switching valve cannot reach the open position. Purge flow is blocked and the EVAP system cannot vent the canister.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Switching Valve Control Circuit Performance
records.descriptionEn: The evaporative switching valve — used on multi-path EVAP systems to route purge or pressure-test flow — does not respond as expected. Self-test fails because tank pressure does not change in the calibrated direction.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP switching valve cannot close. Tank pressure cannot be isolated for the leak detection test, and purge routing may bypass the canister.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 1 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 2 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

records.titleEn: Throttle Actuator Control System Ice Blockage Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The throttle actuator on bank 2 cannot move because of ice formation - typical for very cold ambient temperature with humid intake. Engine de-ices on warm-up.
symptomsEn: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

records.titleEn: SCR Inducement Forced Engine Shutdown
records.descriptionEn: The SCR inducement strategy (mandatory regulatory measure to enforce AdBlue refilling and emissions compliance) has reached the final stage and shut down the engine. Refill AdBlue and clear inducement fault to restart.

causes.labelEn: AdBlue tank empty or out of compliance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The valve that routes engine coolant to heat the AdBlue lines is stuck closed - AdBlue lines do not warm up and may freeze in cold weather, blocking dosing.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler B Efficiency Below Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The temperature drop across EGR cooler B is below the calibrated threshold - cooler is fouled with soot, has internal scaling, or coolant flow is restricted. Recirculated gas reaches the intake hotter than designed, increasing NOx and combustion temperatures.

causes.labelEn: Cooler fouled with soot or scaled

records.titleEn: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP switching valve cannot open when commanded. Purge or test flow cannot reach the appropriate path and the leak monitor aborts.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Vent Valve Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: The evaporative emission system vent valve does not close on command. The ECU detects that the evap system cannot hold pressure or vacuum because the canister is permanently vented to atmosphere.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP Canister Vent Valve Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The vent valve at the canister end of the EVAP system cannot open. Without ambient air entering the canister, fresh fuel cannot purge the stored vapors and refueling may trigger ORVR issues. Common with rusted or rodent-damaged vent valves.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The ECU determines that the hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 1 no longer holds enough HC during cold start to meet emission targets. Often due to ageing or thermal damage.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 2 - which traps HC during cold-start until the main catalyst lights off - is degraded; HC slip during cold start is above the calibrated threshold.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The valve that admits coolant flow to the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - cooling cannot be enabled and EGR temperatures stay too high.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Low
