records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The DPF on bank 2 needs regeneration more often than calibrated. Possible causes are an oil-burning engine, fuel-injector leak, short-trip operation, or a sensor offset.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Regenerations on bank 2 take longer than calibrated to complete - typically a low EGT during the cycle (cold weather, short trips) or a partially aged catalyst before the DPF.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.labelEn: Switching valve stuck open by carbon or corrosion
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The switching valve on bank 1 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.labelEn: Switching valve stuck closed by carbon
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: The switching valve on bank 2 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary-air pump does not run when commanded during cold start. Often a seized pump (after exhaust back-feed corroded the impeller), a blown fuse, or a failed relay.

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
records.descriptionEn: The secondary-air pump continues to run after the cold-start window, when the ECU has commanded it off. Usually a stuck-closed relay welding the pump permanently to battery voltage.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck Off (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 secondary air pump does not deliver air when commanded. The catalyst light-off process is delayed and cold-start emissions rise.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck On (Bank 2)
records.descriptionEn: Bank 2 secondary air pump runs continuously. Either a stuck-on relay or a shorted control output keeps the pump powered when it should be off.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The secondary air injection system on bank 1 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

records.titleEn: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The secondary air injection system on bank 2 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The differential pressure across the DPF is below the calibrated minimum even at higher loads. Often a sign of a damaged or missing filter substrate, or a leak in the sensing line.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Offset
records.descriptionEn: At engine off, the DPF differential pressure sensor does not return to zero within the allowed offset window. The static offset is too large to be ignored.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 1 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes.labelEn: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P244C with the EGT too high - regeneration paused to protect filter substrate from melt damage.

causes.labelEn: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 2 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes.labelEn: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: Same as P244D on bank 2.

causes.labelEn: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: EVAP System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP switching valve does not respond to commands as expected. The valve is mechanically stuck or unable to switch between purge and vent paths, blocking proper leak diagnosis.
symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: EVAP System Switching Valve Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The EVAP switching valve - which directs vapor flow between purge and leak-detection paths - is stuck in the closed position. The diagnostic cycle cannot complete.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptomsEn: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general electrical fault on the DPF differential-pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid pressure reading the ECU cannot estimate soot load and may inhibit regeneration.

causes.labelEn: Sensor sample hoses clogged with soot

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The DPF differential-pressure sensor produces a value that is electrically valid but does not match expectations — for example a non-zero reading with engine off or no change between idle and load.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the DPF differential-pressure sensor signal line is below the lower threshold. Typically a short to ground or an open in the supply line.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the DPF pressure sensor line exceeds the upper threshold. Usually a short to supply or an open ground on the sensor.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The DPF differential-pressure sensor delivers an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a chafed wiring section that breaks contact during temperature or vibration.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler Performance
records.descriptionEn: The EGR cooler does not lower exhaust gas temperature as expected — typically internal coolant fouling, a partial blockage, or a cracked cooler that mixes coolant with exhaust gas.

records.titleEn: DPF Regeneration Duration
records.descriptionEn: The DPF regeneration cycle takes longer than the calibrated maximum. The ECU sets this code when the soot load is not being burned off within the expected window — common after many short trips or with degraded post-injection.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
records.descriptionEn: Active DPF regenerations are being requested more often than the calibration window allows. Indicates that soot accumulates faster than the filter can burn it off — typically due to short-trip use, leaking injectors, or excessive engine oil consumption.

causes.labelEn: High engine oil consumption (turbo seals, valve stems)

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Open Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 - routes EGR around the cooler during cold-start to keep cabin and engine warm-up fast - has an open control circuit.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P245A with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.labelEn: Bypass valve sticking due to soot

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Low Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: A general circuit fault on the secondary differential pressure sensor B across the DPF - measures backpressure for the regeneration strategy.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
records.descriptionEn: Same as P245E with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited Power
records.descriptionEn: The DPF restriction has reached a level that forces the ECU to limit engine power. The driver must allow a forced regeneration or have the filter serviced before normal power is restored.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited
records.descriptionEn: The DPF restriction has reached the limit defined for forced limited operation. Vehicle behaviour depends on the manufacturer — usually a hard torque cap with a service warning.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation
records.descriptionEn: The DPF differential pressure sensor reports a backpressure rise consistent with excessive soot accumulation. The filter cannot regenerate fast enough, eventually causing limp mode.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction — Soot Accumulation
records.descriptionEn: The estimated soot mass in the DPF has crossed the upper limit and the ECU could not complete a regeneration to bring it back down. Very common on cars used on short trips. Continued driving in this state risks a runaway regeneration that destroys the filter.

causes.labelEn: DPF heavily loaded after multiple aborted regenerations
Differential pressure sensor reading drifted high

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High
records.descriptionEn: The differential pressure across the DPF exceeds the calibrated upper threshold during operation. Indicates severe blockage of the filter element.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The DPF differential pressure sensor signal is implausible compared to engine load and exhaust flow. Either the sensor or the pressure tubes leading to it are at fault.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.descriptionEn: At cold start the SCR system is unable to begin reductant dosing within the required time. Typical cause on diesel cars in winter — frozen AdBlue in the tank or lines, failed tank heater, or a slow-warming SCR catalyst.

causes.labelEn: AdBlue frozen — tank or line heater not working
SCR catalyst slow to reach light-off

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3

records.titleEn: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3

The ECM expects a smooth voltage proportional to ammonia concentration in the tailpipe — sudden jumps, dropouts or noise mean the wiring, connector or sensing element is failing. Used to close-loop the AdBlue/DEF dosing strategy.

causes.labelEn: Chafed or vibrating harness near the exhaust
Aged ceramic sensor element drifting under heat cycles

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The heater inside the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor warms the sensing cell to operating temperature so it can read tailpipe ammonia. The ECM detects an open in the heater control circuit — no current flows when the heater should be active, so the sensor never reaches its working point and SCR closed-loop control is suspended.

causes.labelEn: Burnt-out heater winding inside the sensor
Failed heater driver stage in the dosing module

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The heater control circuit of the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor reads below the expected voltage range. Either the wiring is shorted to ground or the heater driver in the SCR/dosing module is stuck low. The sensor element never warms up, NH3 readings stay invalid and the SCR strategy falls back to open-loop dosing.

causes.labelEn: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Internal short across the heater element
Low-side driver pulled down in the control module

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The heater control circuit of the NH3 slip sensor reads above the expected voltage range. Typically a short to battery voltage or a heater driver stuck high — duty-cycle control is lost, the heater either runs continuously or not at all, and the sensor element risks overheating before the ECM disables it.

causes.labelEn: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Performance
records.descriptionEn: The heater of the NH3 slip sensor is electrically intact, but the warm-up profile or steady-state temperature feedback does not match the ECM model. The sensor takes too long to reach operating temperature or drifts away from setpoint, so SCR closed-loop control is delayed or held off.

causes.labelEn: Poor thermal contact between heater and sensing cell

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The supply rail that powers the NH3 slip sensor electronics (typically 5 V or 12 V from the dosing/SCR module) is out of tolerance. Without a stable supply the sensor cannot deliver a valid ammonia reading, and the ECM disables the closed-loop SCR strategy.

causes.labelEn: Failing supply rail inside the dosing module

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage drops below the lower limit. Usually a partial short to ground in the supply line, an undersized ground path with high resistance, or an internal supply collapse in the SCR/dosing module. Sensor output is held invalid until the supply recovers.

causes.labelEn: High-resistance ground at the SCR module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage rises above the upper limit. Either the supply is shorted to battery voltage or an internal regulator in the dosing module has failed open. The sensor electronics may be damaged if the condition persists, so the ECM disables the input.

causes.labelEn: Supply line shorted to battery voltage
Failed voltage regulator in the dosing module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Calibration Memory
records.descriptionEn: The NH3 slip sensor stores its individual calibration coefficients in non-volatile memory (EEPROM/flash). The ECM cannot read valid calibration values — either checksum fails, the memory is empty after replacement, or communication with the sensor electronics is broken. Without the trim values the raw ammonia reading is unreliable.

causes.labelEn: New sensor installed but not coded/learned to the ECM
Corrupted calibration memory after voltage drop
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

records.titleEn: NH3 Sensor Processor Performance
records.descriptionEn: The microcontroller inside the smart NH3 slip sensor reports an internal performance fault — failed self-test, watchdog reset, or out-of-range plausibility checks. The sensor cannot guarantee its output value, the ECM marks the channel invalid and disables SCR closed-loop control on this branch.

causes.labelEn: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

records.titleEn: Control Module Wake-up Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The wake-up line that brings a sleeping ECU back from low-power mode is open. Many networks use a dedicated hardware wake-up wire (door-latch trigger, terminal 15, CAN wake-up) so modules can stay asleep with the ignition off. Without it, the module either fails to wake up at start-up or stays awake and drains the battery.

causes.labelEn: Broken wake-up wire or unplugged connector
Failed wake-up input stage in the module
Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The wake-up input on the control module reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted wake signal. The module either keeps waking up unnecessarily and drains the battery, or it cannot distinguish a real wake event from the stuck low level.

causes.labelEn: Door, hood or terminal switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Control Module Wake-up Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The wake-up input reads above the expected range — typically a short to battery voltage. The module sees a permanent wake-up request, never enters sleep mode and drains the battery while parked.

causes.labelEn: Wake-up wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: EGR Temperature/Charge Air Cooler Temperature Correlation
records.descriptionEn: After a long key-off soak both the EGR temperature sensor and the charge-air cooler outlet temperature sensor must read approximately the same ambient temperature. The ECM compares them and detects an implausible delta. One of the sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or is exposed to a heat source the model does not know about.

causes.labelEn: Residual heat in the charge-air cooler after a hot soak

records.titleEn: Reductant Tank Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
records.descriptionEn: After a long key-off soak the AdBlue/DEF tank temperature and the fuel tank temperature should read close to each other (both at ambient). The ECM detects an implausible spread, which usually means one of the two sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or has a heat source nearby that the plausibility model does not account for.

causes.labelEn: One temperature sensor drifting outside tolerance
Recently active reductant tank heater warming the tank above ambient

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: The pre-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level — for example after a fuel cut or transition into low-load. Aged ceramic cells, soot deposits or condensation inside the sensor protective tube slow the diffusion of NOx to the measuring element.

causes.labelEn: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The post-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level. Same failure mechanism as the upstream sensor — aged element, soot or condensate — but post-catalyst the consequence is a degraded SCR conversion-efficiency monitor.

causes.labelEn: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Open
records.descriptionEn: On systems that inject HC dosing fuel or AIR-assisted reductant into the aftertreatment, a purge valve clears the line after each dosing event. The ECM detects the valve stuck open — pressure or flow does not build up against a closed valve, so the dosing line cannot be charged. Common on diesel HC-doser hardware (DPF regen support).

causes.labelEn: Mechanically stuck open valve from soot or coking
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment HC dosing or reductant purge valve is stuck closed. The ECM commands purge but the line is not cleared, leaving residual fluid that can foul nozzles or freeze in cold weather. Subsequent dosing events also fail because backpressure does not match the model.

causes.labelEn: Stuck closed by deposits or seized armature
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault in the control circuit of the aftertreatment fuel/air purge valve. The ECM cannot drive the valve coil according to plausibility checks — open, short or unexpected feedback voltage. Until cleared, dosing line purge is suspended.

causes.labelEn: Failed driver stage in the dosing module

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The valve coil is electrically intact, but the response (current rise time, return-current decay, position feedback) does not match the ECM model. Typical for solenoids losing magnetic strength after long thermal cycling, or armatures with increased friction from coking.

causes.labelEn: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a failed low-side driver. The valve is energised continuously when it should be off, or the diagnostic feedback voltage is pulled below threshold.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground/return path. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve.

causes.labelEn: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: The PM (soot) sensor heater is driven by a current-limited stage so it can burn off accumulated soot before each measurement. The driver reports current or junction temperature above the safe limit and disables itself. Often a partial short across the heater or sensor element after coolant intrusion.

causes.labelEn: Partial short across the heater element
Driver overheating due to poor cooling on the module

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter A Incorrect
records.descriptionEn: The ECM identifies the installed particulate filter A as the wrong part — backpressure signature, regeneration efficiency or coded part-number do not match the application. Common after a non-OEM aftermarket DPF or a wrong-application replacement.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: SCR Catalyst Incorrect
records.descriptionEn: The ECM identifies the installed SCR catalyst as the wrong part — NOx conversion efficiency, NH3 storage capacity or coded part-number do not match the expected application. Typical after fitting a non-OEM SCR brick or after a coding error following replacement.

causes.labelEn: Incorrect or non-OEM SCR catalyst installed

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Reductant Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: The temperature of the AdBlue/DEF in the dosing system exceeds the safe limit — risk of thermal decomposition (NH3/biuret formation) and clogged dosing nozzles. Often caused by a stuck-on tank heater, a stalled coolant return or proximity to a hot exhaust component.

causes.labelEn: Heat soak from exhaust or engine bay

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The L-terminal feedback line from the alternator (charging warning lamp circuit) reads below the lower limit. The lamp may stay on, and battery voltage may drift if regulation feedback is also affected.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The L-terminal feedback from the alternator reads above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. Charging diagnostics cannot run cleanly.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Charging System Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an out-of-range charging system voltage without specifying high or low. Indicates a generic charging fault that requires further sub-code investigation.

records.titleEn: Charging System Voltage Low
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects that battery voltage during operation stays below the regulated target. The alternator output is insufficient to maintain charge under load, eventually leading to battery depletion.

records.titleEn: Charging System Voltage High
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a battery voltage above the regulated upper limit. The voltage regulator is not limiting alternator output, risking damage to electronic modules and battery overcharge.

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal
records.descriptionEn: The ECM/PCM monitors the main switched battery feed (typically terminal 15 / ignition-switched supply via the main relay). A general fault is reported — either the input is missing entirely or it does not match the expected timing relative to ignition state. Engine may not start or stay running.

causes.labelEn: Blown fuse on the ECM power feed
Corroded connector pin at the ECM

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The switched-battery input to the ECM/PCM is present, but the level or transient behaviour is out of plausibility — sagging during cranking, slow ramp-up after main-relay close, or noisy. Often caused by aged main relay contacts or a weak battery feed under load.

causes.labelEn: Aged main relay contacts with rising contact resistance
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Low
records.descriptionEn: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads below threshold while the ignition is on. Either the main relay does not close, the supply wire is broken or shorted to ground, or the battery is too low. Engine usually fails to start until the input recovers.

causes.labelEn: Main relay does not pull in

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal High
records.descriptionEn: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads above the upper threshold. Most often caused by a charging system overvoltage (failed alternator regulator) or wrong jump-start procedure. Sustained high voltage risks damaging ECU electronics.

causes.labelEn: Improper external power source or jump-start

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects sporadic interruptions of its supply voltage. The fault is set when supply drops below a threshold for short periods, often during cranking or due to a poor connection.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the engine oil level sensor circuit. The ECM cannot read a plausible level signal (analog level, ultrasonic or capacitive sender). Without a valid level reading the ECM disables oil-low warnings and dynamic service-interval calculation.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the oil pan

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The oil level sensor is electrically intact, but the level reading is implausible — for example a constant value across drives, jumps that cannot match real oil consumption, or readings outside the design range. Often a contaminated or aged float/ultrasonic sender.

causes.labelEn: Foaming oil under high RPM masking the level
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit, typically a short to ground or an open at the reference end of the sender. The ECM treats the input as invalid and ignores oil-low warnings until the circuit is repaired.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit, typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return. Pegged at maximum, the ECM cannot distinguish full from invalid and disables the level monitor.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The oil level signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually loose contacts, vibration cracks at the sender or oil sloshing on bumpy roads. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when the noise pattern exceeds the diagnostic limits.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Too Low
records.descriptionEn: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks bearing damage and oil-pump cavitation, so the ECM sets a critical warning, may reduce torque and asks the driver to add oil immediately.

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The voltage reported on the main power relay sense line for the engine controller does not match expectation. The ECU may shut down too early or stay awake too long, draining the battery.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The sense (feedback) line that lets the ECM verify the main power relay has actually closed shows intermittent dropouts. The ECM expects to see battery voltage on this line whenever the relay is energised — short losses suggest aged contacts, vibration or chafed wiring.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The Event Data Recorder (EDR / black box) request line — used by the ECM or restraint module to trigger the EDR to capture pre-crash data — is open. The ECM cannot trigger an event capture, so any subsequent crash event would not be recorded reliably.

causes.labelEn: Open request wire or unplugged module
Failed input stage in the EDR
Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The EDR request line reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees a constant request (which it cannot service) or cannot pulse the line high to fire a real event capture.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The EDR request line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line back low to release the request, so the EDR may either ignore further requests or sit in a permanent triggered state.

causes.labelEn: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault in the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. Sensor B usually monitors the low-side or compressor-suction pressure (in addition to high-side sensor A). The ECM cannot read a plausible value and disables variable compressor control to avoid evaporator freeze-up or overpressure.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B is electrically intact, but its reading does not match the system model — for example pressures that do not fall when the compressor is off, do not change with ambient temperature, or contradict pressure sensor A. Often a refrigerant charge issue or a contaminated sensor.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads below the lower limit. Either a short to ground in the signal wire, an open reference voltage at the sensor, or an internal short. The ECM ignores the reading and disables A/C closed-loop control until the circuit recovers.

causes.labelEn: Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or an overpressure event briefly pegging the sensor. ECM disables variable compressor control to protect the system.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Request A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the A/C compressor request input A. This input tells the ECM that the HVAC controller wants the A/C compressor engaged. With the input invalid, the ECM cannot enable the compressor clutch — A/C does not cool, idle-up compensation is not applied.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted A/C request wire
HVAC module not transmitting the request

records.titleEn: PTO Enable Switch Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The Power Take-Off (PTO) enable switch input to the ECM is open. PTO is used on trucks and work vehicles to drive auxiliary equipment from the engine — without a valid enable signal the ECM refuses to enter PTO operating mode, idle speed control changes do not apply.

causes.labelEn: Open switch wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: PTO Enable Switch Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently closed switch. The ECM either sees PTO enabled when the operator has not requested it, or cannot release the PTO mode after work.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: PTO Enable Switch Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the input low, so the switch state is unreadable and PTO mode is locked out for safety.

causes.labelEn: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The PTO engine-shutdown command line is open. This safety input lets a connected work attachment (or operator switch) request an immediate engine shutdown — for example when an interlock is opened on a stationary aerial work platform. With the line broken, the safety shutdown cannot be commanded.

causes.labelEn: Broken shutdown wire or unplugged work attachment
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted shutdown request. The ECM may treat this as an active shutdown command and refuse to start or keep the engine running while in PTO mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line low to acknowledge a shutdown request, so the operator-side safety chain is effectively disabled.

causes.labelEn: Shutdown wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: A/C Request A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The A/C compressor request input A reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees A/C demanded all the time (cannot release idle-up, raises fuel use) or cannot distinguish a real request from the stuck low level.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Request A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The A/C request input A reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the line low to read switch state, so the A/C compressor request is treated as invalid and the clutch stays disengaged.

causes.labelEn: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: A/C Request B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the second A/C request input B. Many vehicles have two HVAC zones, a rear evaporator request, or a redundant request line — input B carries that signal. With the input invalid, the ECM cannot honour zone B compressor demand or rear-evap operation.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted A/C request wire B
HVAC module not transmitting request B

records.titleEn: A/C Request B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The A/C request input B reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted request. Same effect as input A stuck low, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: A/C Request B Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The A/C request input B reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the switch state, request B is treated as invalid.

causes.labelEn: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor circuit. The reservoir stores manifold or pump-generated vacuum for systems like brake booster, EGR actuators or HVAC dampers. Without a valid reading the ECM disables vacuum-pump duty cycle control.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The vacuum reservoir pressure sensor is electrically intact, but the reading does not match the model — vacuum that does not build up after pump activation, does not bleed off when consumers draw, or stays at one value. Often a partly clogged hose, a leaking reservoir or an aged sensor.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — usually a short to ground or open reference. The ECM disables vacuum pump control until the input recovers.

causes.labelEn: Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — usually a short to reference voltage or open signal return. ECM disables vacuum pump control to avoid overshooting.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: The sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — loose connector, vibration, or chafed harness. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when noise exceeds limits.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the engine oil quality sensor — typically a capacitive/dielectric sensor that estimates oil aging from permittivity, viscosity proxies and conductivity. With no valid reading the dynamic service-interval algorithm falls back to the fixed-interval default.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor electrode after long use

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The oil quality sensor is electrically intact, but the readings do not match the model — for example permittivity that does not change after an oil change, or shifts inconsistent with km/h driven. Often a contaminated electrode or oil that does not fit the sensor calibration.

causes.labelEn: Oil grade outside the sensor calibration range
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — typically a short to ground in the signal line or an internal short across the sensor electrode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The oil quality sensor signal jumps or drops out — usually a loose connector at the oil pan, an oil-soaked harness or vibration cracks at the sensor housing.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Level Too High
records.descriptionEn: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level above the safe maximum after sensor checks pass. Overfilling raises foaming, blow-by and crankcase pressure — and on diesels with regen-by-injection, fuel dilution can drive the level up by itself. The ECM warns the driver and may flag for service.

causes.labelEn: Fuel dilution from incomplete DPF regeneration

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the ignition switch run position input. The signal indicating that the ignition is in the run position is missing or implausible.

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck low — short to ground or a permanently closed contact. The ECM cannot tell when the operator releases the switch from Run, so accessory and crank logic gets confused.

causes.labelEn: Run input wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect when the operator turns the switch back to off/accessory, so module sleep and accessory power timeouts do not work correctly.

causes.labelEn: Run input wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the ignition switch On/Start (terminal 50 / crank) input. The ECM uses this signal to know when the starter is energised — without it the ECM cannot raise fuel and timing for cranking, the engine struggles to start or stalls right after.

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see crank request when the key is at rest, blocking accessory functions or causing unexpected starter cut-off logic.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the crank state, modules dependent on this signal are unable to time their wake-up correctly.

causes.labelEn: On/Start wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the ignition switch accessory (terminal 75 / ACC) input. ACC tells the ECM that radio, fans, accessory loads should be powered without the engine running. With the input invalid, the body controller may misjudge accessory power timing.

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The ACC input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see ACC active continuously and refuse to enter sleep, draining the battery.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The ACC input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot detect when the operator releases the switch from ACC, accessory power timeouts do not work.

causes.labelEn: ACC wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the low-pressure fuel system sensor — typically the lift-pump or pre-supply pressure sensor that monitors the rail feeding the high-pressure pump. With no valid reading, the ECM cannot verify that lift pressure is sufficient for HP-pump intake.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor

records.titleEn: PTO Sense Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The PTO sense (engagement feedback) line is open. This input tells the ECM whether the PTO clutch or driveline is actually engaged after a request — it closes the loop on the PTO enable command. With it broken, the ECM cannot confirm engagement and refuses to ramp up to PTO speed setpoints.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: PTO Sense Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The PTO sense circuit is electrically intact, but the engagement feedback does not match the command. The ECM requests engage and sees no engaged feedback (or vice versa) within the expected time window — drive-line slip, sticky clutch, or a mis-adjusted limit switch.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: PTO Sense Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The PTO sense input reads stuck low — short to ground or limit switch stuck closed. The ECM may see PTO continuously engaged.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: PTO Sense Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The PTO sense input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect engagement.

causes.labelEn: Sense wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: PTO Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The PTO sense signal jumps or drops out — usually loose connectors, a chattering limit switch, or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Oil Deteriorated
records.descriptionEn: The oil quality monitor concludes that the engine oil has reached the end of its useful life — based on permittivity, soot content, fuel dilution and total operating hours. The ECM requests an oil change before the next regen cycle to prevent accelerated bearing wear.

causes.labelEn: High DPF regeneration load with fuel dilution

records.titleEn: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects a general fault in the low-pressure fuel system pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid signal the ECU cannot verify lift-pump pressure or fuel rail pre-pressure.

records.titleEn: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The signal of the low-pressure fuel sensor does not match the expected value during operation. Pressure does not rise as expected when the lift pump is commanded.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The low-pressure fuel system sensor signal voltage is above the upper limit. Either a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or a sensor reading pegged high after an internal failure. The HP-pump pressure-control strategy falls back to default.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Power Demand Signal Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the power demand input signal used to coordinate accessory loads (e.g. AC compressor, alternator load). The signal is missing or implausible.

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal A
records.descriptionEn: The ECU detects an invalid torque-management request signal A from another control unit (e.g. transmission, ESP, ABS) on the CAN bus. Cooperative torque control cannot be performed as expected.

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECM receives torque-management requests from other modules (TCM during shifts, ABS/ESC during traction events, hybrid controller). Input A is electrically intact but its values do not match the system model — out-of-range steps, jumps, or persistent values that other modules cannot confirm.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Low
records.descriptionEn: Torque management input A reads stuck low — analog short to ground or message stuck at minimum value. The ECM cannot trust the request and falls back to a safe default.

causes.labelEn: CAN message stuck at minimum value

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal A High
records.descriptionEn: Torque management input A reads stuck high — analog short to reference voltage or message stuck at maximum value. The ECM rejects the request to avoid running unintended high-torque commands.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
CAN message stuck at maximum value

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal B
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the second torque-management request input B. Used when more than one module needs to request torque adjustments — typically TCM on input A and ABS/ESC on input B, or chassis vs powertrain. With B invalid, only the A-side request is honoured.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wire / invalid CAN message

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Input B is electrically intact but the values are implausible — same failure mode as the A-side performance fault, applied to the second torque-management channel.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The PTO speed-selector switch 1 input is open. This switch lets the operator pick a preset PTO operating speed (idle, 800, 1200 rpm, etc.). With the input broken, the ECM cannot apply any operator-selected speed and falls back to a default speed.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The selector input is electrically intact but the value is implausible — multiple positions asserted at once, or a value that cannot map to any of the configured speed presets. Often a sticky multi-position switch or a contaminated rotary contact.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes.labelEn: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The PTO speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Hood Switch Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the engine hood (bonnet) switch circuit. The hood switch tells the body controller and (on hybrids) the high-voltage system that the hood is open — used for security, alarm and HV-safety interlock. With the input invalid, alarm logic and HV interlock fall back to a safe state.

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Low
records.descriptionEn: Torque management input B reads stuck low — short to ground or message at minimum. ECM rejects the request, only A-side is used.

records.titleEn: Torque Management Request Input Signal B High
records.descriptionEn: Torque management input B reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or message at maximum. ECM rejects the request to avoid unintended high-torque commands.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit input A. This input lets external safety functions (immobilizer, hybrid HV interlock, anti-theft) override the throttle or cut fuel delivery. With the input invalid the safety override is unreliable, so the ECM falls back to its safe default — typically inhibit asserted to err on the side of safety.

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The throttle/fuel inhibit A signal is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the immobilizer reports OK, or de-asserted while a hybrid HV interlock is active. The ECM cannot trust the signal.

causes.labelEn: Requesting module sending an inconsistent value
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted. ECM may treat it as continuous inhibit and refuse normal operation.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. ECM cannot read the inhibit state and falls back to the safe default.

causes.labelEn: Inhibit wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the engine coolant level sensor/switch circuit. Many vehicles use a simple float-switch in the expansion tank, others use a continuous-level analog sensor. With the input invalid the ECM cannot warn for low coolant before overheating starts.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the expansion tank

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The coolant level sensor is electrically intact, but the readings are implausible — for example a level that does not move at all over many drive cycles, or jumps that cannot match real coolant loss. Often a stuck float, contaminated electrode or air-locked sensor.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Coolant level sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Coolant level sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The second PTO speed-selector switch input is open. Switch 2 typically encodes a binary or multi-bit code together with switch 1 — together they select one of several preset PTO speeds. With switch 2 broken, only the half of the bit pattern is available, so several presets cannot be reached.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: PTO speed selector switch 2 is electrically intact but its value does not match a valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted, or values that do not map to any preset.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes.labelEn: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: PTO speed selector 2 signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: A/C Request A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The A/C request input A is electrically intact, but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the HVAC controller reports off, toggling rapidly, or sustained while compressor pressures cannot support it. The ECM disables A/C clutch engagement until the input becomes plausible.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Level Low
records.descriptionEn: The coolant level monitor reports the engine coolant below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks overheating, head warping and head-gasket failure. The driver is warned and the ECM may reduce engine power until the level is restored.

causes.labelEn: External coolant leak (hose, radiator, water pump)
Head gasket leaking coolant into combustion

records.titleEn: A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
records.descriptionEn: The A/C / HVAC control module has requested the ECM to illuminate the malfunction indicator (MIL) because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is stored in the HVAC module — this code only signals that the ECM has honoured the request.

causes.labelEn: Internal fault in the HVAC module — read its DTCs

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor A — the feedback sensor on the wastegate or VGT actuator (often a contactless Hall sensor). Without valid position feedback the ECM cannot close the loop on boost control and falls back to open-loop duty cycle.

causes.labelEn: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element after thermal cycling

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The position feedback sensor on the variable-geometry or wastegate turbocharger actuator is not communicating or is implausible. Without position feedback, boost control runs in default mode and power is reduced.

causes.labelEn: Wiring open or chafed near turbo

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open reference voltage at the sensor.

causes.labelEn: Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage in the signal line or open signal return.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The turbocharger actuator position sensor reports a value, but it does not track commanded vane or wastegate position within tolerance. Often a sticky VTG mechanism due to soot.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The turbocharger position sensor signal is below the lower limit — short to ground or sensor at zero stop.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The turbocharger position sensor signal is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground or sensor failed high.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Charging may not start or interrupts

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Direct Ozone Reduction (DOR) catalysts are coated radiator surfaces or dedicated catalysts that decompose tropospheric ozone passing over the radiator — used for low-emissions vehicles. The temperature sensor monitoring the DOR brick reads stuck low — short to ground or sensor short.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The idle-speed selector input is open. On commercial vehicles this switch lets the operator pick a fast-idle setpoint (for example to keep auxiliary loads supplied). With the input broken, the ECM cannot apply an operator-selected idle speed.

causes.labelEn: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The idle-speed selector input is electrically intact but the value does not match a valid preset — multiple positions or a non-mappable value. Often a sticky multi-position switch.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal at maximum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The idle-speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

records.titleEn: A/C Request B Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: A/C request input B is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — same failure mode as the input A performance fault, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes.labelEn: HVAC module sending inconsistent request B
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return. Without a valid temperature the ECM cannot enable the DOR efficiency monitor.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator pack.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the DOR catalyst deterioration sensor circuit. This sensor estimates the remaining ozone-conversion capacity of the DOR coating — coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by salt or grime, or thermally aged. Without a valid signal the deterioration monitor is disabled.
symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The DOR deterioration sensor is electrically intact but its readings drift or do not match the model — for example a deterioration value that does not move with km/h driven, or moves implausibly fast.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The DOR deterioration sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
records.descriptionEn: The DOR catalyst no longer reduces tropospheric ozone with the required efficiency, based on the deterioration sensor and operating-time model. Coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by road salt and grime, or thermally aged after many heat cycles. Replacing the affected radiator/coating restores function.

causes.labelEn: DOR coating worn off the radiator
Coating contaminated by salt and grime

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit
records.descriptionEn: General electrical fault on the turbocharger/supercharger shaft speed sensor A — a high-frequency Hall or eddy-current sensor on the compressor shaft. The ECM uses turbo speed for overspeed protection (typically 200,000+ rpm) and for closed-loop boost on VGT systems. With no valid speed the ECM limits boost.

causes.labelEn: Aged sensor with reduced output amplitude

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: Turbo speed sensor A is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the model — for example a speed that does not climb when boost rises, drifts away from the air-mass-flow estimate, or jumps. Often blade-fouling, a contaminated sensor tip or aged element.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit/Open
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit that drives the vacuum reservoir control valve (or vacuum pump motor) is open. The ECM cannot energise the actuator, so vacuum is no longer maintained on demand and consumers like brake booster, EGR or HVAC dampers may run out of vacuum.

causes.labelEn: Failed driver in the control module
Pin pushed back out of connector body

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The actuator may be energised continuously when it should be off.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve/motor.

causes.labelEn: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The hood switch is electrically intact, but its state is implausible — for example reporting hood-open while vehicle speed is rising, or rapid toggles. Usually a worn switch with high contact bounce or a misaligned hood actuator.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The hood switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed switch. The body controller may treat the hood as permanently open and refuse to arm the alarm or close the HV interlock.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Hood Switch Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The hood switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The body controller cannot detect when the hood is opened.

causes.labelEn: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open supply.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Turbo speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist on the sensor tip, or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes.labelEn: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

records.titleEn: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
