records.titleEn: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire in the harness.

causes.labelEn: Harness chafed against valve cover or cam carrier
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Serial Number Not Programmed or Incompatible
records.descriptionEn: The engine controller cannot read a valid engine serial number from its non-volatile memory, or the stored value does not match the expected pattern. Calibration sets keyed to the serial number cannot be applied.

causes.labelEn: Replacement ECU not programmed at install

records.titleEn: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1

records.titleEn: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage to actuator group B (e.g. solenoids, valves driven by ECU) is below the calibrated threshold. The affected actuators may be slow or unable to switch.

records.titleEn: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit High

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Injection Pump Timing Offset
records.descriptionEn: The high-pressure injection pump timing is offset from the expected reference. On distributor pumps with a timing solenoid, the actuator does not match the commanded position.

causes.labelEn: Worn timing actuator piston or seal
Stretched pump drive chain or belt

records.titleEn: Injection Pump Timing Calibration Not Learned
records.descriptionEn: The injection pump timing learning routine did not complete successfully. Without learned values, injection timing runs from default tables and combustion is suboptimal.

causes.labelEn: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or unstable conditions
Timing actuator drift outside learning window

records.titleEn: Injection Pump Fuel Calibration Not Learned
records.descriptionEn: The injection pump fuel quantity calibration did not complete successfully. Without learned fuel calibration, AFR runs from default tables and emissions or smoke can rise.

causes.labelEn: Learning routine aborted by other DTC or unstable conditions
Fuel quantity solenoid drift outside learning window

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit / Open

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low

records.titleEn: Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit High

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit / Open

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Performance

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

symptomsEn: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the aftertreatment glow plug control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the aftertreatment glow plug control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment glow plug element itself is open. No current flows even with the relay closed.

causes.labelEn: Glow element burnt out from age or HC overload
Corroded terminal at the plug body

symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Performance
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment glow plug heats but exhaust temperature does not rise as expected. Combustion of injected HC may not start.

causes.labelEn: Aged glow plug heats slowly or unevenly
HC supply from 7th injector below required

symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment glow plug current is below expected. Either the element is partially open or supply is undersized.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment glow plug current is above expected. Internal short reduces resistance. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Internal short in the glow plug element
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptomsEn: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The coolant bypass valve A responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected. Possibly stuck partially open or contaminated bore.

causes.labelEn: Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The position sensor on the coolant bypass valve A returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of bypass position is lost.

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The bypass valve A position sensor reading does not correlate with commanded position. Sensor drift or worn linkage.

causes.labelEn: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn linkage between actuator and valve
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The bypass valve A position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The bypass valve A position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The bypass valve A position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop/Minimum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: During self-calibration the bypass valve A position sensor never reached the minimum mechanical stop. The position reference cannot be zeroed.

causes.labelEn: Sediment prevents valve from reaching minimum stop
Sensor not aligned with valve shaft

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Maximum Stop Performance
records.descriptionEn: During self-calibration the bypass valve A position sensor never reached the maximum mechanical stop.

causes.labelEn: Sediment prevents valve from reaching maximum stop
Sensor not aligned with valve shaft

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck/Open
records.descriptionEn: The coolant bypass valve A is stuck in the open position. Coolant always bypasses the radiator, leading to overheating under load.

causes.labelEn: Valve seized open by sediment or wax

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The controller cannot drive the second coolant bypass valve. The associated cooling sub-loop cannot be regulated.

causes.labelEn: Open coil in bypass valve solenoid

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Low

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Range/Performance

Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed
records.descriptionEn: The coolant bypass valve A is stuck closed. Coolant cannot bypass the radiator during warm-up so warm-up takes longer and emissions in the warm-up phase rise.

records.titleEn: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Sensor Performance
records.descriptionEn: The internal transmission range sensor inside the control module (used for redundancy on shift-by-wire systems) does not match the external sensor reading.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Internal Control Module Clutch Pedal Performance
records.descriptionEn: The internal clutch pedal interpretation logic in the control module does not match the external clutch switch state. Manual transmission start interlock or stop-start enable can misbehave.

causes.labelEn: Signal corruption between switch and ECU

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The controller cannot drive the exhaust flow control valve A (used for exhaust acoustics, EGR boost, or aftertreatment heating).

records.titleEn: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is below the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is above the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Chassis Control Module 1 Requested MIL Illumination
records.descriptionEn: A chassis control module (typically active suspension, AWD coupling, or steering controller) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.labelEn: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

records.titleEn: Chassis Control Module 2 Requested MIL Illumination
records.descriptionEn: A second chassis control module has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.labelEn: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The controller cannot drive the main electric coolant pump. Without flow the engine and aftertreatment will overheat under load.

causes.labelEn: Broken control wire to the pump

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Performance/Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: The main electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run.

causes.labelEn: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Overspeed/Air In System
records.descriptionEn: The coolant pump speed feedback is higher than the commanded value with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.labelEn: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The integrated controller of the smart coolant pump reports a system voltage out of operating range.

causes.labelEn: Weak battery sags voltage under pump load

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage Low
records.descriptionEn: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage below operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.

causes.labelEn: Weak battery sags voltage under load

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage High
records.descriptionEn: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage above operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.

causes.labelEn: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Load dump transient after disconnecting a heavy load

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module Over Temperature
records.descriptionEn: The smart coolant pump controller has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow.

causes.labelEn: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptomsEn: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated supply voltage line to the coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is below operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Weak battery sags under pump current
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is above operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The mechanical clutch on a belt-driven coolant pump (used to disengage the pump for fast warm-up) cannot be driven. Pump always engaged so warm-up takes longer.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Performance/Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: The coolant pump clutch is commanded on but does not engage. Coolant flow is missing under load, leading to overheating.

causes.labelEn: Worn friction surfaces enlarge air gap
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The coolant pump clutch remains engaged when commanded off. Pump runs continuously, slowing warm-up and increasing parasitic load.

causes.labelEn: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit Low

records.titleEn: Engine Sound Control A Circuit High

records.titleEn: Starter Relay B Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The control circuit for the secondary starter relay (used on twin-starter heavy diesels or stop-start systems with a dedicated stop-start starter) returns no usable signal.

records.titleEn: Starter Relay B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Starter Relay B Circuit High

records.titleEn: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit / Open

symptomsEn: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Control Module System Voltage
records.descriptionEn: The alternative fuel control module reports a system voltage out of operating range. CNG, LPG, or hydrogen fuelling can be disabled until voltage is in spec.

causes.labelEn: Weak battery sags voltage under load

records.titleEn: Engine Sound Control B Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The second active sound generator (B) cannot be driven.

causes.labelEn: Open output stage in the sound amplifier

records.titleEn: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Low

records.titleEn: Starter Relay A Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The first starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.

causes.labelEn: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Starter Relay A Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: The first starter relay does not close when commanded on. Starter motor cannot crank, the engine will not start.

causes.labelEn: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Starter Relay B Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: The second starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor B remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.

causes.labelEn: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Starter Relay B Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: The second starter relay does not close when commanded on. The associated starter motor cannot crank.

causes.labelEn: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The controller cannot drive the third electric coolant pump. Cooling demand of the connected loop (often hybrid power electronics or battery cooling) is not satisfied.

causes.labelEn: Broken control wire to the pump

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.labelEn: Internal short in pump motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Supply Voltage Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The dedicated supply voltage line to the third coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Stuck/Stalled
records.descriptionEn: The third coolant pump is commanded on but the rotor does not turn. Sediment, frozen coolant, or a foreign object jams the impeller.

causes.labelEn: Impeller jammed by sediment or debris
Pump motor seized by bearing failure

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Control Module Overtemperature
records.descriptionEn: The smart controller of the third coolant pump has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow around the pump electronics.

causes.labelEn: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel around pump blocked by debris

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Overspeed/Air in System
records.descriptionEn: The third coolant pump speed feedback is higher than commanded with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.labelEn: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, which slows engine warm-up and can degrade cold-start emissions.

causes.labelEn: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, slowing engine warm-up and degrading cold-start emissions.

causes.labelEn: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: A/C Compressor Internal Control Module Performance
records.descriptionEn: The internal control module of an electrically driven A/C compressor (typical on hybrid and BEV vehicles) reports an internal performance fault. Compressor capacity may be reduced or shut down.

causes.labelEn: Internal fault in compressor inverter electronics
Software error in compressor control logic
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptomsEn: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

records.titleEn: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Performance
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust flow control valve A responds to commands but the resulting flow or back-pressure does not match expectations. Worn flap or carbon coking on the bore.

records.titleEn: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: During controller auto-configuration the expected throttle input on bank 2 was not detected. Configuration cannot complete and the second throttle path cannot be used.

causes.labelEn: Broken signal wire from throttle B2
Hardware variant mismatch — sensor not installed

records.titleEn: Transmission Friction Element A Apply Time Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The transmission control module measured an apply time for friction element A (clutch or band) outside the calibrated window. Indicates worn clutch material, low line pressure, or a degrading shift solenoid.
symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Transmission Friction Element B Apply Time Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The time required to apply friction element B (a clutch or band inside the automatic transmission) is outside the expected window. Either too long (worn clutch, low pressure) or too short (sticky valve, mis-calibration).

causes.labelEn: Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Transmission Friction Element C Apply Time Range/Performance

records.titleEn: Shift Solenoid F
records.descriptionEn: A general fault in shift solenoid F (the sixth gear-selection solenoid in 6-speed and higher transmissions). Detected through electrical resistance, hydraulic response, or downstream gear engagement check.

causes.labelEn: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Shift Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: Shift solenoid F is commanded on but does not produce the expected hydraulic response. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic apply circuit blocked.

causes.labelEn: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Apply circuit blocked by debris in valve body
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Shift Solenoid F Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: Shift solenoid F stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected gear stays applied so the transmission cannot shift correctly.

Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptomsEn: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Shift Solenoid F Electrical

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
records.descriptionEn: The transmission disengaged mechanically without a corresponding command. The vehicle can free-wheel, which is a safety concern. Often a hydraulic or hardware fault inside the gearbox.

causes.labelEn: Clutch piston seal failure releases gear

records.titleEn: Hydraulic Power Unit Leakage
records.descriptionEn: The transmission hydraulic power unit (pump + accumulator) has detected a pressure drop that suggests internal leakage. Pressure cannot be held during shifts.

causes.labelEn: Worn or hardened seals in the valve body
Worn hydraulic pump cannot maintain pressure

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D

causes.labelEn: Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off
records.descriptionEn: Pressure control solenoid D is commanded on but does not produce the expected pressure. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic feed restricted.

Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D Stuck On
records.descriptionEn: Pressure control solenoid D stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected hydraulic circuit stays pressurised.

causes.labelEn: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D Electrical
records.descriptionEn: The TCM detects an electrical fault on transmission pressure control solenoid D. Hydraulic pressure cannot be modulated as expected, causing harsh or slipping shifts.

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D Intermittent
records.descriptionEn: Pressure control solenoid D shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults. Loose connector or marginal coil.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit / Open
records.descriptionEn: The control line to pressure control solenoid D is open. The solenoid cannot be driven.

records.titleEn: Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The current through pressure control solenoid D does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Coil resistance drift or high-resistance contact.

causes.labelEn: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The position sensor that confirms the park pawl A engagement state reads below the lower diagnostic threshold. Without confirmed park engagement the shift-by-wire controller cannot release the brake hold.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Park Pawl Position Sensor A Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The position sensor for park pawl A reads above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The redundant park pawl position sensor B reads below the lower diagnostic threshold. Redundancy for the park-engagement check is lost.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Park Pawl Position Sensor B Circuit High

Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

records.titleEn: Transmission Adaptive Values Not Learned

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Too High Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 1 exceeds the calibrated maximum. Common causes are clogged DPF, restricted exhaust path, or stuck exhaust brake/back-pressure valve.

causes.labelEn: DPF clogged with soot or ash

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Too High Bank 2

causes.labelEn: DPF clogged with soot or ash

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Too Low Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 1 falls below the calibrated minimum. Common causes are leaks upstream of the sensor, missing DPF substrate, or sensor calibration drift.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Too Low Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The exhaust pressure measured on bank 2 falls below the calibrated minimum. Common causes are leaks upstream of the sensor, missing DPF substrate, or sensor calibration drift.

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 does not show the expected slow steady-state behaviour after the catalyst. Either the sensor is degraded or the catalyst itself behaves abnormally.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
records.descriptionEn: The optional third oxygen sensor on bank 1 (typically downstream of a second catalyst) returns implausible values during long-term monitoring.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 reacts too slowly or shows insufficient signal swing during closed-loop fuel control.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 2
records.descriptionEn: The rear oxygen sensor on bank 2 shows abnormal behaviour during long-term plausibility evaluation. Often a sign of an aged sensor or weakened catalyst.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 3
records.descriptionEn: The third oxygen sensor on bank 2 (after a second catalyst stage on some vehicles) returns implausible values. Often related to sensor aging or mechanical exhaust leak upstream.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 1, where present, returns implausible values during long-term plausibility evaluation. Used on multi-stage aftertreatment systems.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 4
records.descriptionEn: The fourth oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns values outside the expected long-term performance window during plausibility checks.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

records.titleEn: O2 Sensor Negative Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 3
records.descriptionEn: The ECM detects a negative voltage on the signal line of oxygen sensor 3 on bank 1. This is unusual for narrow-band sensors and often indicates a short to a negative reference, ground offset, or a wide-band sensor wired incorrectly.

causes.labelEn: Signal wire shorted to negative reference
Ground offset between sensor and ECM

Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.labelEn: Vaporizer not yet at operating temperature

causes.labelEn: Injectors aged - flow drift across cylinders
Fuel rail pressure drifts during pulse

records.titleEn: Injection Pulse Performance

causes.labelEn: Injectors aged - flow drift across cylinders
Fuel rail pressure drifts during pulse

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
records.descriptionEn: The required adaptation offset for the exhaust pressure control valve A position exceeds the calibrated learning window. Mechanical wear or sensor drift beyond compensation.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Supply Low
records.descriptionEn: The supply voltage to the exhaust pressure control valve A actuator is below the expected window. Fuse blown, supply wire shorted, or upstream regulator fault.

records.titleEn: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Driver Current/Temperature Too High
records.descriptionEn: The output driver for the exhaust pressure control valve A reports current or junction temperature above its protection threshold. Stalled actuator or short-circuit fault.

records.titleEn: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
records.descriptionEn: The reductant (DEF/AdBlue) quality sensor signal drops out or jumps intermittently. Loose connector, dilution noise, or ground reference offset.

causes.labelEn: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Vehicle Conditions Incorrect for Particulate Matter Sensor Regeneration
records.descriptionEn: The ECM detects that the vehicle is not operating in conditions suitable for the periodic PM sensor regeneration cycle. The sensor element cannot be cleaned and soot-mass measurement is paused.

causes.labelEn: Driving cycle too short for regen conditions

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump A Stuck/Stalled
records.descriptionEn: Coolant pump A reports a stuck/stalled condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit
records.descriptionEn: Coolant pump A reports a supply voltage circuit condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump A Control Module Overtemperature
records.descriptionEn: Coolant pump A reports a control module overtemperature condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

causes.labelEn: Ambient or under-bonnet temperature too high

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump B Underspeed

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump C Underspeed
records.descriptionEn: Coolant pump C reports a underspeed condition. Coolant circulation through the affected loop cannot be commanded reliably.

records.titleEn: Coolant Pump D Underspeed

records.titleEn: Engine Coolant Pump Stuck/Stalled
records.descriptionEn: The engine coolant pump is mechanically stuck or has stalled. Coolant circulation through the engine is severely reduced or absent.

records.titleEn: Starter/Generator Mechanical Performance
records.descriptionEn: The hybrid control module detects that the integrated starter/generator does not deliver the expected mechanical torque or speed for the commanded operation. Belt slippage, bearing wear, or coupling fault.

records.titleEn: Catalyst Feedgas Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECM detects that the exhaust gas composition reaching the catalyst (feedgas) deviates from the calibrated profile. Pre-cat O2 measurement and air-fuel control are inconsistent with engine operation.

causes.labelEn: Long-term fuel trim drifted out of nominal range

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: Particulate Filter Feedgas Performance
records.descriptionEn: The ECM detects that the exhaust gas composition reaching the particulate filter (feedgas) deviates from the calibrated profile. Soot input rate cannot be modelled correctly, affecting regen scheduling.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedance - SCR NOx Catalyst Performance
records.descriptionEn: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to the SCR NOx catalyst. Conversion efficiency is degraded — aged substrate, sulphur poisoning, or thermal damage.

causes.labelEn: SCR catalyst substrate aged or contaminated
Thermal damage from prior over-temperature event

symptomsEn: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence - Empty Reagent Tank
records.descriptionEn: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to an empty reductant tank. SCR cannot dose AdBlue/DEF.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence - Interruption of Reagent Dosing Activity
records.descriptionEn: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to interruption of reductant dosing. The injection valve, pump, or supply line is impaired.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence — Insufficient Reagent
records.descriptionEn: The SCR system has detected that NOx emissions exceed the legal limit and the cause is traced to insufficient AdBlue/DEF dosing. Modern emission regulations require this fault to be reported separately so that operator-induced misuse (running an empty tank, diluting the fluid) is recorded.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
records.descriptionEn: The upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 returns values that are not plausible for the current operating point. NOx sensors are slow to warm up, sensitive to soot and water, and are a frequent failure on diesel SCR systems.

causes.labelEn: Sensor contaminated with soot or condensate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence — Reagent System Performance
records.descriptionEn: The SCR system has detected that NOx emissions exceed the legal limit and the cause is traced to a performance fault in the reagent dosing system — for example a slow dosing pump, a clogged injector, or a frozen line that is not yet caught by another DTC.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence - Insufficient Reagent Quality
records.descriptionEn: The diesel exhaust aftertreatment system detects elevated NOx levels combined with abnormal reagent (AdBlue/DEF) consumption, indicating that the reagent quality is insufficient or contaminated. Many regions trigger driver inducement (limited restarts).
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence - Insufficient Reagent Consumption
records.descriptionEn: The aftertreatment system detects elevated NOx emissions while reagent (AdBlue/DEF) consumption is below the expected level. Causes include clogged dosing injector, incorrect dosing rate or tampering.
symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: NOx Exceedence - EGR System
records.descriptionEn: NOx emissions are above the legal threshold and the ECU isolates the cause to the EGR system. EGR flow is too low or absent under operating conditions where NOx reduction is required.

records.titleEn: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
records.descriptionEn: The heater sense feedback of NOx sensor 1 on bank 1 reports values that do not match expected operation. The sensor warm-up cycle does not behave as the diagnostic expects.

causes.labelEn: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptomsEn: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Consumption Too Low

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Consumption Too High
records.descriptionEn: The AFCM detects that alternative fuel consumption exceeds the expected value for the active operating mode. Indicates injector leakage, fuel pressure too high, or unmetered fuel loss.

records.titleEn: Alternative Fuel Tank Empty
records.descriptionEn: The AFCM detects that the alternative fuel tank is empty. Bi-fuel vehicles may switch to gasoline operation; mono-fuel vehicles cannot continue without refuel.

records.titleEn: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Performance

records.titleEn: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a high-side voltage fault (short to power) on the cylinder 8 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a high voltage condition in the control circuit of the cylinder 8 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid. A short to voltage or open low-side path causes the driver to read above the expected range, disabling cylinder deactivation requests for cylinder 8.

causes.labelEn: Solenoid or wiring shorted to power

records.titleEn: Cylinder 8 Deactivation
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder 8 deactivation system. Common in V8 engines with active fuel management — cylinder 8 cannot reliably switch state.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Open
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an open hydraulic circuit in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 1. The system uses pressurized engine oil routed through dedicated lifters and oil control valves to collapse valves; an open circuit indicates loss of oil flow or a failed pressure switch.

causes.labelEn: Oil passage blocked or sludge buildup

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a performance fault in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit used for cylinder deactivation. Oil pressure response or timing is outside the expected window during deactivation events, often caused by viscosity issues, internal leaks or worn lifters.

causes.labelEn: Incorrect oil viscosity or aged oil
Internal oil leak in deactivation circuit

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Low
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected low oil pressure in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit responsible for cylinder deactivation. Below threshold pressure the lifters cannot collapse and the system disables further deactivation requests on bank 1.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 High
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an excessively high oil pressure or stuck-on signal in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit for cylinder deactivation. Either a stuck oil control valve, a blocked relief path, or a shorted pressure switch is reporting permanently high pressure.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Open
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an open hydraulic circuit in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 2. Loss of oil flow, a failed oil pressure switch or a disconnected oil control valve prevents the system from deactivating cylinders on bank 2.

causes.labelEn: Oil passage blocked or sludge buildup

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a performance fault in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit used for cylinder deactivation. Oil pressure response or actuation timing falls outside the expected window during deactivation events on bank 2, often caused by viscosity issues, internal leaks or worn switching lifters.

causes.labelEn: Incorrect oil viscosity or aged oil
Internal oil leak in deactivation circuit

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Low
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected low oil pressure in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit responsible for cylinder deactivation. Below the calibrated threshold the switching lifters cannot collapse and cylinder deactivation on bank 2 is disabled until pressure recovers.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 9 Deactivation
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder 9 deactivation system. Found on V10/V12 engines with cylinder deactivation — cylinder 9 cannot reliably switch state.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 High
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an excessively high oil pressure or stuck-on signal in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit for cylinder deactivation. A stuck oil control valve, a blocked relief path or a shorted pressure switch is reporting permanently high pressure on bank 2.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 1 Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an electrical fault in the cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch circuit on bank 1. The switch confirms that hydraulic pressure has reached the level required to collapse the switching lifters; without a valid signal the system disables deactivation.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 1 Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a rationality fault between commanded oil pressure and the bank 1 cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch state. The switch fails to change state at the expected pressure threshold during deactivation transitions.

causes.labelEn: Oil control valve slow to respond

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 2 Circuit
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an electrical fault in the cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch circuit on bank 2. Without a valid signal the module cannot confirm that hydraulic pressure has reached the level needed to deactivate cylinders on bank 2.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Oil Pressure Switch Bank 2 Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a rationality fault between commanded oil pressure and the bank 2 cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch state. The switch fails to change state at the expected pressure threshold during deactivation transitions on bank 2.

causes.labelEn: Oil control valve slow to respond

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 1 Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an open circuit at the bank 1 cylinder deactivation solenoid. The solenoid routes oil pressure to the switching lifters; an open circuit prevents activation and the system disables deactivation requests on bank 1.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 2 Control Circuit Open
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an open circuit at the bank 2 cylinder deactivation solenoid. The solenoid routes oil pressure to the switching lifters on bank 2; an open circuit prevents activation and the system disables deactivation requests on bank 2.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 10 Deactivation
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder 10 deactivation system. Found on V10/V12 engines — cylinder 10 cannot reliably switch state.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 1 Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a low voltage condition at the bank 1 cylinder deactivation solenoid control circuit. A short to ground or low-side driver fault prevents proper actuation of the bank 1 deactivation hydraulic path.

causes.labelEn: Solenoid or wiring shorted to ground

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 1 Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a high voltage condition at the bank 1 cylinder deactivation solenoid control circuit. A short to power or open low-side path causes the driver to read above the expected range, disabling deactivation requests on bank 1.

causes.labelEn: Solenoid or wiring shorted to power

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 2 Control Circuit Low

causes.labelEn: Solenoid or wiring shorted to ground

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Solenoid Bank 2 Control Circuit High

causes.labelEn: Solenoid or wiring shorted to power

records.titleEn: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Performance
records.descriptionEn: Per-cylinder exhaust valve control on cylinder 11 does not respond as commanded. Mechanical issue at the deactivation actuator for that cylinder.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 11 exhaust valve control voltage below expected range — short to ground. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

records.titleEn: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
records.descriptionEn: Cylinder 11 exhaust valve control voltage above expected range — short to power or open ground. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.labelEn: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

records.titleEn: Cylinder 11 Deactivation

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation System Performance Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected that the cylinder deactivation system on bank 1 is not performing as expected. Closed-loop monitoring of pressure response, valve timing or misfire counters during transitions indicates the system fails to deactivate or reactivate cylinders within calibrated limits.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation System Performance Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected that the cylinder deactivation system on bank 2 is not performing as expected. Closed-loop monitoring of pressure response, valve timing or misfire counters during transitions indicates the system fails to deactivate or reactivate cylinders within calibrated limits.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an implausible signal from the bank 1 cylinder deactivation position sensor. Modern systems use a Hall-effect or inductive sensor to confirm switching lifter position; a fault prevents safe deactivation transitions.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected an implausible signal from the bank 2 cylinder deactivation position sensor. The sensor confirms switching lifter position; without a valid signal the module cannot safely command deactivation transitions on bank 2.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 1 Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected the bank 1 cylinder deactivation position sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not change as expected during commanded deactivation transitions. Mechanical drag, sensor drift or contamination is the typical cause.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Position Sensor Bank 2 Range/Performance
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected the bank 2 cylinder deactivation position sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not change as expected during commanded deactivation transitions. Mechanical drag, sensor drift or contamination is the typical cause.

records.titleEn: Cylinder 12 Deactivation

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation System Bank 2

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Pressure Sensor Bank 1
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a fault with the bank 1 cylinder deactivation pressure sensor. Newer variable displacement systems use an analogue oil pressure sensor in addition to or in place of the legacy switch; a fault disables closed-loop deactivation control on bank 1.

records.titleEn: Cylinder Deactivation Pressure Sensor Bank 2
records.descriptionEn: The engine control module has detected a fault with the bank 2 cylinder deactivation pressure sensor. The analogue oil pressure sensor is used to verify the deactivation hydraulic state; a fault disables closed-loop deactivation control on bank 2.

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus
records.descriptionEn: A general fault on the high-speed CAN bus has been detected. This bus typically connects powertrain modules (ECM, TCM, ABS) at 500 kbit/s and a fault disables communication between them, often triggering multiple secondary DTCs in other modules.

causes.labelEn: Open circuit in CAN bus wiring
Terminating resistor failed (not 60 ohms across bus)

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus Performance
records.descriptionEn: The high-speed CAN bus is functional but performance is degraded — frame errors, bit errors or excessive bus load have been detected. Communication may be intermittent rather than completely lost, leading to sporadic warning lamps.

causes.labelEn: Corrosion or poor contact in CAN connectors

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Open
records.descriptionEn: The CAN-High line of the high-speed bus is open. Without the differential pair, the controller cannot decode any traffic and reports loss of all participating modules at once. Often follows a wiring repair, accident damage, or a corroded connector pin.

causes.labelEn: CAN-High wire broken or pin pushed back
Harness damage after repair or accident

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Low
records.descriptionEn: The CAN-High signal stays below its valid voltage window. Common cause is a short to ground on the CAN-H wire or a transceiver that pulls the line down. The bus stops working until the offending node is isolated.

causes.labelEn: Internal transceiver failure on a node
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) High
records.descriptionEn: The CAN-High line is held above its valid voltage range, usually because of a short to battery voltage. Bus communication collapses for every connected module.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Open
records.descriptionEn: The CAN-Low wire of the high-speed bus is open. The differential signal can no longer be evaluated correctly, so all bus participants report communication loss simultaneously.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Low
records.descriptionEn: The CAN-Low line is shorted to ground or held below its valid recessive level. The differential pair cannot transmit data and the bus is effectively dead.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

records.titleEn: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) High
records.descriptionEn: The CAN-Low signal is held above its valid range, typically because of a short to battery voltage on the CAN-L wire. Bus communication is lost for every node sharing this segment.

causes.labelEn: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module

Typical causes are loss of power or ground at the module, an open or shorted CAN/LIN bus wire, a connector fault, or an internal module failure.

causes.labelEn: CAN wiring to satellite radio broken
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptomsEn: Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults
